name: YCB Object and Model Set
evaluates: Grasping, pick-and-place, in-hand, bimanual and assembly on 77 everyday objects that vary in shape, size, texture, weight and rigidity
improves: Gives labs a shared physical object set plus a protocol template, so results from different robots can be compared
setup: 77 purchasable household objects with RGB-D scans and models, plus a protocol template. No robot is fixed.
scale: 77 objects
note: The official protocols page was unreachable during the survey; current purchase availability was not checked.

name: ACRV Picking Benchmark (APB)
evaluates: Complete shelf-picking systems (perception plus manipulation)
improves: Reproducible scene setup: 42 objects, a widely available shelf, and stencils that fix object arrangement
setup: 42 objects, a widely available shelf, and stencils for object placement. No robot is fixed.
scale: 42 objects
note: Semantic Scholar lists the year as 2016.

name: RA-L 2020 Special Issue protocols (14)
evaluates: One protocol each for gripper strength and repeatability, grasp resilience, grasp planning, bin picking, Rubik's cube, small-parts assembly, bimanual cloth, semi-deformable objects, in-hand manipulation, aerial manipulation, and handover
improves: The absence of any widely adopted manipulation benchmark; every paper had to use standard objects, a common protocol template, and baseline results
setup: 14 written protocols that use standard object sets and a shared benchmark template.
scale: 14 protocols

name: GRASPA 1.0 / GRASPA-fying the Panda
evaluates: Grasp planning pipelines on a robot arm
improves: The lack of a common protocol and metrics for grasping; scores are normalized to each platform's workspace and payload so different robots can be compared
setup: Printable layouts and metrics normalized to platform limits; first run on iCub, later packaged for the Franka Panda.

name: NIST Assembly Task Boards (ATB 1–4)
venue: Boards since 2017 · protocol paper IEEE RA-L 2020
evaluates: Small-parts assembly systems: peg insertion, gear meshing, connectors, nut threading, belts, cable routing, wire harnesses
improves: Standard fabricable boards with CAD, scoring and analysis guidelines, so industrial assembly results are measured the same way everywhere
setup: Four task boards with CAD, STL files, fabrication instructions and scoring metrics. No robot is fixed.
scale: 4 boards
note: Whether boards can currently be ordered was not checked.

name: Box and Blocks Test benchmark
evaluates: Speed of pick-and-place in clutter (blocks moved per unit time)
improves: Borrows a clinical dexterity test, giving a robot-agnostic score that is compared against human norms
setup: Three protocols of increasing difficulty based on the clinical Box and Blocks Test; baselines on Barrett WAM and Franka Panda.
scale: 3 protocols

name: Benchmarking In-Hand Manipulation
evaluates: Planning and control for changing the pose of a held object using fingers, the environment, or both
improves: Common task definitions (initial and goal poses on YCB meshes) and a shared pose-error metric
setup: Initial and goal object poses with fingertip locations on YCB meshes; any hand.

name: Benchmarking Bimanual Cloth Manipulation
evaluates: Tablecloth spreading, towel folding and dressing, at several difficulty levels with quality measures
improves: Runs on any bimanual platform with standardized, easy-to-buy cloth objects
setup: Standard, easy-to-acquire cloth objects; any bimanual platform.
scale: 3 tasks

name: Household Cloth Object Set (HCOS)
evaluates: Deformable-object manipulation: folding, piling, table setting, bed making
improves: A cloth object set that can be distributed among research groups, the cloth counterpart of a rigid object set
setup: A distributable set of household cloth objects with RGB-D and object scans.
note: Current distribution status was not checked.

name: ICRA 2024 Cloth Competition dataset
evaluates: Grasp selection for unfolding garments
improves: Turns a one-off competition into a reusable dataset and offline benchmark (679 attempts, 34 garments)
setup: Recorded on a shared robot during the live competition.
scale: 679 unfolding attempts, 34 garments, 11 teams

name: Cluttered Environment Picking Benchmark (CEPB)
evaluates: Perception, planning, control and grasping in sequential bin picking
improves: Separate protocols per pipeline stage for warehouse-style picking, on a fixed 40-object set
setup: 40 objects drawn from YCB, the ACRV Picking Benchmark and T-LESS.
scale: 40 objects

name: EGAD!
evaluates: Grasping systems across a controlled range of shape complexity and grasp difficulty
improves: 49 3D-printable objects, so anyone can reproduce the test set without sourcing products
setup: 49 3D-printable evaluation objects.
scale: 49 objects
note: Author list was recalled from memory, not re-verified.

name: SceneReplica
evaluates: Full grasping pipelines (perception, planning, execution) on pick-and-place in clutter, with failures attributed to each stage
improves: Replicable scenes without markers: operators rebuild each scene by overlaying a reference image on the live camera
setup: 16 YCB objects in 20 tabletop scenes, rebuilt by overlaying a reference image; Fetch mobile manipulator.
scale: 20 scenes × 5 objects = 100 pick-and-place trials

name: Robothon / euROBIN task board (DR.J)
evaluates: Speed and completion of electronic task-board subtasks (e-waste disassembly, device testing)
improves: The board scores itself with onboard electronics and reports to a web dashboard, building a shared performance database
setup: Open-hardware task board under $200 whose microcontroller verifies subtasks and timing; more than 55 boards deployed.
note: Runs locally, but scores are reported to a web dashboard.

name: AHAP
evaluates: Grasping ability of anthropomorphic hands across 10 grip patterns
improves: A hand-level protocol with 25 household objects
setup: 25 household objects, 26 tasks, 10 grip patterns.
scale: 26 tasks
note: Venue not verified.

name: Benchmarking Multi-Object Grasping
evaluates: Grasping several objects at once from piles and surfaces
improves: Three protocols for a capability that single-object grasp benchmarks do not cover
setup: Three protocols for pile and surface scenarios.
scale: 3 protocols
note: Preprint under journal review.

name: GRAB
evaluates: Grasping in clutter for food-waste sorting, across three gripper types and four clutter levels
improves: Graspability metrics that describe pre-grasp conditions, on a domain existing benchmarks skip
setup: Three gripper modalities and four randomized clutter levels.
scale: 1,750 grasp attempts
note: Preprint.

name: REPLAB
evaluates: Learned grasping (plus an RL reaching baseline)
improves: Cost and reproducibility: a self-contained arm, camera and workspace for about $2,000 that assembles in hours
setup: Self-contained cell (arm, camera, workspace) for about $2,000 that assembles in a few hours.
scale: 92k grasp attempts

name: ROBEL
evaluates: Reinforcement learning for dexterous manipulation (D'Claw) and locomotion (D'Kitty) on real hardware, including hardware-safety metrics
improves: Low-cost open-source robots so results can be replicated across institutions
setup: Open-source low-cost robots: D'Claw (9-DoF hand) and D'Kitty (quadruped).
note: Replication across institutions is the authors' claim.

name: TriFinger
evaluates: Dexterous manipulation by control and learning methods
improves: An inexpensive open platform that can run autonomously and safely for long periods
setup: Open-source three-finger platform for about $5,000 with 1 kHz control.
note: The hosted cluster version is listed under Real Robot Challenge.

name: DeepClaw
evaluates: Tic-Tac-Toe, bin clearing and jigsaw tasks across three hardware configurations
improves: A reconfigurable cell and shared task hierarchy that accept arms, grippers and cameras from different vendors
setup: Reconfigurable cell that hosts arms, grippers and cameras from several vendors.
scale: 3 tasks on 3 hardware configurations

name: RB2
evaluates: Learning algorithms on pouring, scooping, zipping and insertion
improves: Cross-lab variance: the same experiment differed by 20% between labs, so local results are pooled into one global ranking instead of comparing absolute numbers
setup: Tasks inspired by a clinical hand-assessment procedure, run in two labs and pooled into one ranking.
scale: 4 task families
note: Exact hardware was not verified.

name: FurnitureBench
evaluates: Long-horizon, complex furniture assembly (grasping, inserting, screwing)
improves: A reproducible real-world setup: 3D-printed furniture, a setup guide and systematic initialization, checked by 10 independent reproductions
setup: Franka Panda, RealSense cameras, 3D-printed furniture, and an initialization tool with three randomness levels.
scale: 8 furniture tasks, 5,100 demonstrations (219.6 h)
note: 10 independent reproductions with performance gaps under 16% (author-reported).

name: FMB
evaluates: Multi-stage, contact-rich functional manipulation (grasping, repositioning, insertion, assembly), including held-out objects
improves: 3D-printable objects with stated tolerances, a large dataset, and per-skill trial protocols
setup: Franka Panda, four RealSense D405 cameras, 3D-printed objects at 1–2 mm tolerance.
scale: 66 printable objects, 22,550 trajectories

name: RAMP
evaluates: Assembly that needs both manipulation and planning (beams joined with pegs into goal structures)
improves: Parts that are 3D-printed or easy to obtain, with CAD and a digital twin
setup: 3D-printed beams and pegs, AprilTags, and a digital twin.
note: Adoption outside the originating lab was not verified.

name: IndustReal
evaluates: Sim-to-real transfer of RL policies for contact-rich assembly
improves: Releases the hardware and software tools needed to reproduce the system
setup: Released hardware and software tools for sim-to-real assembly.
note: Kit contents were not independently verified.

name: REASSEMBLE
evaluates: Contact-rich assembly and disassembly (pick, insert, remove, place) learned from multimodal data
improves: A dataset built on NIST Task Board 1, so it inherits that board's physical standard
setup: Multimodal recordings (event cameras, force-torque, audio, multi-view RGB) on NIST Task Board 1.
scale: 4,551 demonstrations, 17 objects
note: A dataset that inherits NIST's standard, not a new protocol.

name: HomeRobot OVMM
evaluates: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation: pick any object in an unseen home and place it where commanded
improves: A paired sim and real benchmark on one low-cost mobile manipulator (Hello Robot Stretch)
setup: Hello Robot Stretch, with paired simulation and real homes.
scale: Real-world baseline success 20%

name: THE COLOSSEUM
evaluates: Robustness of policies to perturbations in color, texture, size, lighting, distractors, physical properties and camera pose
improves: Systematic generalization testing, with printable objects to replicate the perturbations on a real robot
setup: Simulation benchmark plus 3D-printable objects that replicate the perturbations on a real Franka.
scale: 20 tasks, 14 perturbation axes
note: The main artifact is simulation; the real part is a validation study (sim–real R² 0.614).

name: λ (LAMBDA)
evaluates: Language-conditioned, long-horizon, multi-room mobile pick-and-place, with a focus on data efficiency
improves: A sim and real benchmark for a setting where tabletop benchmarks do not apply
setup: Simulated and real settings; hardware is not stated in the abstract.
scale: 571 demonstrations
note: Semantic Scholar lists the venue year as 2024.

name: VLA-REPLICA
evaluates: VLA and imitation policies on 10 tabletop tasks, in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenes
improves: Cost and cross-setup reproducibility: a roughly $1,050 cell with fixed lighting, calibrated cameras and overlay resets, offered as an alternative to remote evaluation
setup: SO-101 arm, RealSense D455, a light box with 5600 K LEDs, AprilTag camera calibration and overlay resets; about $1,050 in total.
scale: 10 tasks, 500 demonstrations, 50 ID + 40 OOD scenes × 5 trials
note: Two independently built setups scored 0.49 vs 0.48 (ID) and 0.55 vs 0.50 (OOD). Preprint.

name: Benchmarking VLA Models on SO-101
evaluates: How VLA policies fail and whether they recover, on four tasks
improves: Goes beyond success rate with a failure taxonomy and recovery-aware metrics; defines a common SO-101 action space
setup: SO-101 arm with a common action space.
scale: 4 tasks, 20 trials per model and task
note: Preprint.

name: GM-100
evaluates: Breadth of skill: 100 detail-oriented tasks on two bimanual platforms
improves: Task coverage; the authors frame it as a first step toward a "robot learning Olympics"
setup: Agilex Cobot Magic and Dobot Xtrainer; object purchase links and template videos.
scale: 100 tasks, 13,000+ teleoperated trajectories
note: Results are being released gradually. Preprint.

name: ATOM-Bench
evaluates: Atomic skills and whether they compose: 30 atomic tasks and 24 held-out compositional tasks
improves: Diagnoses where compositional failures come from (Compositional Failure Share), with mask-guided placement and fixed test seeds
setup: Franka Panda with Robotiq 2F-85 (single-arm) and Agilex Cobot Magic (dual-arm); mask-guided object placement.
scale: 30 atomic + 24 compositional tasks, 2,700 physical rollouts
note: Single-site results. Preprint.

name: LongBench
evaluates: Long-horizon tasks, split into those that need memory of earlier context and those that do not
improves: Stage-wise scoring that separates the mechanisms behind long-horizon failure
setup: ARX-R5 arm with replication documents; a central platform also accepts remote submissions.
scale: 10 tasks, 1,000+ real episodes
note: Preprint.

name: UMI-Bench 1.0
evaluates: Policies trained on UMI-style handheld-gripper data, using wrist cameras only
improves: One local protocol covering data collection, scene reset, execution, logging and task-factor analysis
setup: FastTouch arm, wrist RGB only, a 5 cm acrylic grid board, and a JSON file per scene.
scale: 10 tasks × 50 episodes
note: Preprint.

name: Experiences from Benchmarking VLA Models
evaluates: VLA policies on a mobile bimanual robot under spatial and object shifts
improves: Adds time-to-success and instruction-adherence metrics next to success rate
setup: ALOHA Mobile.
scale: 4 tasks
note: A single-lab study more than a community benchmark.

name: DuoBench
evaluates: Bimanual coordination in four categories: asymmetric support, joint manipulation, sequential handoff, parallel execution
improves: Stage-based scoring and real-world task recipes with printable assets
setup: FR3 Duo with 3D-printed assets (STL files released).
scale: 11 tasks (4 reproduced on real hardware), 200 real episodes
note: Stage tracking is manual; no second-site results. Preprint.

name: BusyBox
evaluates: Affordance generalization: whether a policy can still operate switches, sliders, buttons and dials when the modules are rearranged
improves: An instrumented, 3D-printed box that reports its own state, giving automatic success detection
setup: Six 3D-printed, rearrangeable modules run by a Raspberry Pi Zero; Mobile ALOHA.
scale: 1,993 teleoperated trajectories
note: No second-site results. Preprint.

name: POMDAR
evaluates: Dexterity of anthropomorphic robot hands across 18 manipulation and grasping tasks, scored against a human baseline
improves: A fully 3D-printed test apparatus for comparing hand designs
setup: Test apparatus made on consumer 3D printers; run by teleoperating an anthropomorphic hand.
scale: 18 tasks (12 manipulation, 6 grasping)
note: Depends on teleoperation, so it measures hand and operator together.

name: TactiDex
evaluates: Tactile-guided dexterous manipulation
improves: A dataset aligning whole-hand tactile signals with motion and object state, plus standard metrics
setup: Tactile dataset with standard metrics.
scale: 49 objects, 757 interaction sequences
note: No physical reproduction protocol is evident.

name: Peg-in-Bench
evaluates: High-precision insertion across peg shapes and clearances (0.1, 1 and 3 mm)
improves: A modular, printable insertion kit with specified tolerances
setup: Resin-printed pegs and holes (0.05 mm resolution) at 0.1, 1 and 3 mm clearance.
note: No baselines yet. Preprint.

name: Industrial Dexterity Benchmark
evaluates: Industrial tasks: datacenter cable plugging, cable-harness routing, planetary gearbox assembly
improves: Three open boards with CAD, bill of materials and scoring
setup: Three boards with open CAD, bill of materials and scoring; Franka FR3.
scale: 3 boards, 48 trials per configuration
note: Preprint.

name: RoboArena
evaluates: Generalist policies on open-ended tasks and scenes chosen by evaluators, on the DROID setup
improves: Scalability of centralized evaluation: a network of labs runs double-blind pairwise comparisons and a ranking model aggregates them; model weights stay private
setup: DROID platform (Franka Panda, Robotiq 2F-85, ZED cameras) at eight institutions; submitters host their own inference server.
scale: 612 pairwise comparisons (4,284 episodes) over 7 policies in the paper
note: The live leaderboard could not be read directly during the survey.

name: AutoEval
evaluates: Generalist policies on a few Bridge tabletop tasks
improves: Human labor: learned success detection and learned resets let a cell run around the clock with almost no supervision
setup: WidowX 250 cells in Bridge scenes, with a VLM success classifier and a learned reset policy.
scale: About 500 episodes per cell per day; 4 public tasks
note: The site lists its public tasks as available until January 1, 2026.

name: RoboChallenge Table30 / V2
evaluates: VLA policies on 30 tabletop tasks across four robot types, per-task and generalist tracks; V2 adds multi-task, zero-shot and out-of-domain tests
improves: Online access to a real robot fleet at scale without handing over model weights
setup: Fleet of UR5, Franka Panda, Cobot Magic ALOHA and ARX-5 robots; a remote-robot API keeps weights with the user.
scale: 30 tasks × 10 rollouts; success rate plus a 0–10 progress score
note: The V2 baseline table was not verified.

name: ManipulationNet
evaluates: Physical skills (peg-in-hole, cable management, grasping in clutter) and embodied reasoning (language-conditioned tabletop tasks, block arrangement) on any robot
improves: Realism, accessibility and authenticity together: standard kits are mailed out, tasks run locally, and a server verifies results
setup: Standard kits are mailed to teams and run on any robot; a client reports to a server that issues verification challenges.
scale: Two tracks; 30+ participating teams
note: Paper baselines are labeled preliminary.

name: RoboDojo-RealEval
evaluates: Generalist policies on long-horizon, precision, memory and generalization tasks across three bimanual robots
improves: A unified sim and real suite with remote evaluation and double-blind scoring by three evaluators
setup: ARX X5, Piper and Piper X bimanual robots; policy server; local deployment or remote evaluation.
scale: 18 real tasks × 10 trials
note: Preprint.

name: ManipArena
evaluates: Tabletop execution, tabletop semantic reasoning and mobile manipulation, each with in-domain, shifted and held-out trials
improves: Controlled conditions: a green-screen facility with fixed lighting, cameras and workspace
setup: Green-screen facility with fixed lighting, cameras and workspace.
scale: 20 tasks; 10 trials each with 10-point partial credit
note: Preprint.

name: FolDeX / FoldChallenge
evaluates: Garment folding across more than 10 robot types
improves: A score that combines success, fold quality and efficiency, with held-out garments and double-blind submission
setup: More than 10 robot types; double-blind submission.
scale: 20+ tasks; FoldScore = 35% success + 35% quality + 30% efficiency
note: Preprint.

name: ArmnetBench v0.1
evaluates: Imitation and VLA policies on 12 single-arm and bimanual tasks
improves: Cost per evaluation: low-cost arm cells where one operator supervises several at once
setup: SO-101 cells costing about $359 (single-arm) and $477 (bimanual).
scale: 12 tasks × 7 policies, 2,518 rollouts
note: Not yet open to outside submissions; each task ran on one cell only.

name: PhAIL
evaluates: Speed and throughput of VLA policies on order picking, relative to a human operator
improves: Statistical reporting: time-to-success distributions, confidence intervals, blind scheduling and public run audit
setup: Franka Research 3 with Robotiq 2F-85; open submissions through the positronic framework.
scale: 1 task (bin-to-bin order picking), about 995 rollouts
note: Preprint.

name: Humanoid Everyday cloud evaluation
evaluates: Manipulation policies on humanoid robots across task categories
improves: Access to humanoid hardware: described as the first cloud evaluation platform for humanoids
setup: Unitree G1 and H1; a policy server streams at 30 Hz.
scale: Dataset of 260 tasks and 10.3k trajectories
note: No automatic scene reset.

name: Real Robot Challenge
evaluates: Dexterous manipulation on TriFinger robots; the 2022 edition tested offline RL on pushing and lifting
improves: Access: participants submit code that runs on a remote robot cluster
setup: Eight TriFingerPro robots at MPI-IS; submitted code is scheduled like jobs on a compute cluster.
note: No competition since 2022; cluster access is by application.

name: OCRTOC
evaluates: Table organization (grasping and rearranging objects into a target layout)
improves: Fair comparison on identical robot setups reached through the cloud
setup: Identical real-robot setups reached by cloud upload, with automatic scoring.
scale: 59 teams in 2020
note: No edition found after 2022.

name: CloudGripper
evaluates: Planar pushing and rope manipulation on 32 small remote cells
improves: A shared testbed for large-scale benchmarking and data collection
setup: 32 enclosed cells, each with a low-cost 5-DoF Cartesian arm, gripper and cameras.
scale: 32 cells
note: Testbed for the RGMC 2026 Cloud Robotics track.

name: HALTER
evaluates: Long-horizon manipulation (evaluation tooling, not a benchmark)
improves: Automatic scene reset for long tasks, which earlier automated cells handled poorly
setup: Scene-graph and LLM reset planning on a Franka.
scale: 4 long-horizon tasks; restores the scene in 76% of episodes
note: Evaluation tooling, not a hosted service. Preprint.

name: UniBot World Challenge
evaluates: One model across multiple tabletop tasks (grasping, placing, bimanual coordination)
improves: A hosted leaderboard on real hardware; not yet open
setup: Unitree hardware.
note: Listed as coming soon; no public results.

name: UMI Arena
evaluates: Policies trained on handheld-device data, on eight tasks across three robot arms
improves: Queue-based remote evaluation with held-out tasks
setup: Franka, TX-G2 and OpenArm; submit a Hugging Face model repository to a queue.
scale: 8 tasks (5 public, 3 held-out)
note: Submissions run until 2026-11-02; no results yet.

name: AIRoA Mobile Manipulation Challenge
evaluates: VLA pipelines for mobile manipulation on Toyota HSR
improves: Shared hardware with regular real-robot evaluation rounds
setup: Toyota HSR.
scale: Bi-weekly real-robot rounds, 36 teams

name: RGMC
evaluates: Picking from clutter, in-hand manipulation, human-robot handover, mobile manipulation, assembly on task boards, and a remote cloud-robotics track
setup: On-site evaluation; 2026 adds a remote Cloud Robotics track on CloudGripper.

name: WBCD
evaluates: Bimanual systems (teleoperation plus learning from demonstration) on logistics picking, packing, lab work and pallet loading
setup: On-site physical judging of teleoperation and learning-from-demonstration systems.
note: Assesses teleoperated systems, not autonomous policies alone.

name: Robothon Grand Challenge
evaluates: Speed on a self-scoring electronic task board that teams receive by mail

note: The 2025 winner differs between the results repository and a press release.

setup: 30-day remote phase on teams' own robots, then the top three on site.

evaluates: Unfolding garments on a shared robot
setup: Live evaluation on a shared robot.

evaluates: Industrial assembly (2018) and mixed-goods box packing (2025)
setup: On site.

evaluates: Domestic service tasks; ARM tests autonomous manipulation on a real UR5e

evaluates: Warehouse picking from shelves and bins (discontinued in 2017)

evaluates: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation in a real apartment

evaluates: Bimanual collaboration, with a real round after two simulation rounds

evaluates: Vision-tactile manipulation, with top simulation entries checked on a real tactile platform

evaluates: Manipulation on AgiBot robots (shirt folding, conveyor picking, food preparation); 2026 adds supermarket mobile manipulation

name: LIBERO
evaluates: Language-conditioned tabletop manipulation; built for lifelong-learning knowledge transfer, used by VLA papers as a per-suite fine-tuning success-rate test (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long)
improves: No benchmark isolated transfer of declarative (object, spatial) versus procedural (goal) knowledge in lifelong robot learning with human demonstrations for every task
setup: Robosuite on MuJoCo; Franka Panda arm; agent-view and wrist RGB cameras plus 8-D proprioception; 7-D actions (6-D end-effector delta plus gripper); tasks specified in a PDDL-style language with instructions derived from Ego4D activities
scale: 130 tasks in four suites: LIBERO-Spatial (10), LIBERO-Object (10), LIBERO-Goal (10), LIBERO-100 (LIBERO-90 short-horizon + LIBERO-Long/LIBERO-10); 50 human teleoperated demonstrations per task; common VLA protocol: 4 suites x 10 tasks x 50 episodes (LeRobot uses 10 episodes per task)
policies: OpenVLA (76.5), OpenVLA-OFT (97.1), π0 (94.2, as run by OpenVLA-OFT), π0-FAST (85.5), π0.5 (96.85, openpi), GR00T N1.6 / N1.7, SmolVLA (87.3), X-VLA (98.1), UniVLA (95.2), VLA-Adapter (97.3), VLA-0 (94.7), MemoryVLA, FLOWER, Dita, MMaDA-VLA (98.0), CAC-VLA (98.9), Octo and Diffusion Policy as baselines
status: Most used VLA simulation target; saturated (many four-suite averages of 97-99%; highest found 99.9 with RL post-training). No official leaderboard; third-party aggregate at https://allenai.github.io/vla-evaluation-harness/leaderboard/. Repository last pushed 2025-03
note: Evaluation tasks equal training tasks (no held-out split). LIBERO-PRO (arXiv 2510.03827) reports >90% scores collapsing to 0% under object, layout or instruction changes; a language-blind 0.09B probe scores 92-100% per suite and only 19.8% of SOTA claims are statistically significant (arXiv 2606.04233).

name: CALVIN
evaluates: Long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation: completing chains of five consecutive instructions from onboard sensors, including zero-shot transfer to an unseen environment (ABC→D)
improves: Earlier vision-and-language manipulation datasets had short sequences, simple action spaces and limited language; none tested chained instructions in unseen environments
setup: PyBullet; 7-DoF Franka Panda at a desk with drawer, sliding door, light switch, button and blocks; static and gripper RGB-D cameras, tactile images, proprioception; absolute or relative Cartesian or joint actions at 30 Hz
scale: 34 tasks in four environments (A-D) differing in textures and fixture positions; about 24 h of teleoperated play data (2.4M steps), 1% language-annotated; splits D→D, ABC→D, ABCD→D; 1,000 chains of 5 instructions
policies: X-VLA (4.43 ABC→D), UniVLA (3.80; the separately named Unified VLA reports 4.41), VLA-Adapter (4.42), FLOWER (4.53), Dita (3.61), MMaDA-VLA (4.78), OpenVLA and OpenVLA-OFT (third-party runs), RoboFlamingo, GR-1, DeeR, Seer, MoDE, MDT, 3D Diffuser Actor
status: Standard reporting target; near-saturated on ABC→D (papers report up to 4.78 of 5; official leaderboard tops at 4.53). Leaderboard: http://calvin.cs.uni-freiburg.de/ (served over HTTP only). Repository last pushed 2025-09
note: Official leaderboard lags published results. Audit arXiv 2606.04233: a language-blind probe completes over 3.1 tasks per chain, resampling block poses within the training range drops X-VLA by 1.03, and 19.7% of SOTA claims are statistically significant.

name: RLBench (incl. 18-task PerAct subset)
evaluates: Vision-guided manipulation across 100 hand-designed tasks from reaching to multi-stage tasks; in practice multi-task language-conditioned keyframe policies on the 18-task, 249-variation PerAct subset
improves: Robot learning lacked a large shared task set with motion-planned demonstrations covering reinforcement, imitation, multi-task and few-shot learning
setup: CoppeliaSim (v4.1) via PyRep; Franka Panda; RGB, depth and segmentation from shoulder, front and wrist cameras plus proprioception; PerAct protocol uses four 128x128 RGB-D cameras and next-keyframe end-effector poses executed by a motion planner
scale: 100 tasks with unlimited motion-planned demonstrations; PerAct subset: 18 tasks, 249 variations, 10 or 100 demonstrations per task, 25 evaluation episodes per task
policies: BridgeVLA (88.2% on 18 tasks), HybridVLA (74% on a 10-task subset, with OpenVLA 41%, π0 55%, CogACT 60% as baselines), ActiveVLA; mostly 3D keyframe policies: PerAct, RVT-2 (81.4%), 3D Diffuser Actor (81.3%), SAM2Act (86.8%)
status: Standard target for 3D keyframe policies, secondary for 2D VLAs; 18-task averages now 85-94% (93.7% listed for BridgeVLA++). No official leaderboard. Repository last pushed 2025-01
note: RLBench itself has no real-robot component (PerAct separately ran 7 real tasks). Keyframe-plus-planner results are not comparable with closed-loop VLA results, and VLA papers use differing 10-task subsets; BridgeVLA++ figure taken from a third-party aggregate.

name: Meta-World
evaluates: Multi-task and meta reinforcement learning over 50 Sawyer tabletop tasks; VLA papers use the 50 tasks as a multi-task imitation benchmark grouped into easy, medium, hard and very hard
improves: Earlier meta-RL benchmarks used narrow task distributions that could not test generalization to new tasks
setup: MuJoCo; simulated Sawyer arm; 39-D state observations by default (LeRobot protocol: one 480x480 corner camera plus 4-D state); 4-D actions (3-D end-effector delta plus gripper)
scale: 50 tasks; MT1, MT10, MT50 multi-task sets; ML1, ML10 (10 train, 5 test) and ML45 (45 train, 5 test) meta-learning sets; LeRobot grouping: 28 easy, 11 medium, 6 hard, 5 very hard
policies: SmolVLA (57.3% on 50 tasks), π0 (47.9-50.5%, as run by SmolVLA), TinyVLA (31.6%), FabriVLA (90.0% MT50), Diffusion Policy (10.5%)
status: Secondary VLA reporting target, supported in LeRobot; scores range from 57% to 90% under differing protocols. Maintained by the Farama Foundation (v3; Meta-World+ at NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks; repository pushed 2026-09). No official leaderboard
note: Meta-World+ (arXiv 2505.11289) documents numerous undocumented changes across versions that inhibit fair comparison. VLA use departs from the original RL protocol; the MT50 setting uses fixed object and goal positions.

name: ManiSkill2
evaluates: Generalizable manipulation skills across rigid, articulated and soft-body tasks with object-level variation, for reinforcement and imitation learning from state, RGB-D or point clouds
improves: Earlier manipulation benchmarks had limited object diversity, no soft bodies, slow visual simulation and inconsistent interfaces across task types
setup: SAPIEN for rigid bodies plus a Warp-based GPU MPM simulator for soft bodies; Franka Panda by default, mobile-base robots for cabinet, chair and bucket tasks; state, RGB-D and point-cloud observations; joint or end-effector controllers
scale: 20 task families (e.g., PickCube, StackCube, PickSingleYCB, PickClutterYCB, PegInsertionSide, PlugCharger, OpenCabinetDoor, Pour), 2,000+ object models, 4M+ demonstration frames
real_check: Sim-to-real checks only: a PickCube policy scored 91.0% in simulation and 60.0% on a real ROKAE arm, and Pinch trajectories were compared in simulation and reality; no sim-real ranking correlation.
policies: Dita / Diffusion Transformer Policy (65.8% on a 5-task set), GeoVLA (77.0%), CogACT and OpenVLA-OFT re-implementations (third-party aggregate)
status: Occasional VLA target through 5-task subsets; not saturated (best 5-task average found 77%). Superseded by ManiSkill3; original code kept at tag v0.5.3. No leaderboard
note: No fixed VLA protocol: a third-party aggregate counts 14+ task-subset combinations, with the most common 5-task set covering about 24% of entries. GeoVLA figure taken from that aggregate and a search snippet.

name: ManiSkill3
evaluates: GPU-parallel simulation and rendering for manipulation across 12 task domains (tabletop, mobile manipulation, humanoid, dexterous, drawing/cleaning), used for RL, imitation and fine-tuned VLA evaluation
improves: ManiSkill2 and other simulators were too slow for large-scale visual RL and lacked heterogeneous parallel scenes and real2sim evaluation environments
setup: SAPIEN with GPU-parallel physics and rendering (30,000+ FPS with rendering reported); single-arm, mobile, humanoid and dexterous robots; state, RGB-D and segmentation observations; joint or end-effector controllers
scale: 12 task domains; millions of demonstration frames; VLA use so far: 5 tabletop tasks (PegInsertionSide, PickCube, StackCube, PlugCharger, PushCube) with 5,000 motion-planned trajectories and 250 trials per method
real_check: The task suites report no sim-real correlation; the platform also hosts real2sim digital-twin environments (SIMPLER ports) and sim2real examples, which are catalogued separately.
policies: RDT-1B (53.6% mean), Diffusion Policy (30.2%), OpenVLA (4.8%), Octo (0.0%) on the 5-task set in the RDT repository
status: Actively maintained (repository pushed 2026-08); occasional VLA target through small tabletop subsets; not saturated. No leaderboard
note: Released in 2024, so outside the 2023-or-earlier cut; included because it replaces ManiSkill2 and hosts the RDT benchmark. The RDT evaluation code uses ManiSkill3 (-v1) environments although its README only says ManiSkill.

name: robomimic (robosuite tasks)
evaluates: Offline imitation and offline RL from human demonstrations of varying quality on multi-stage single-arm and two-arm tasks (Lift, Can, Square, Transport, Tool Hang)
improves: No standardized human-demonstration datasets existed to study how data quality, observation modality and hyperparameters affect offline policy learning
setup: Robosuite on MuJoCo; Franka Panda arms; low-dimensional (proprioception plus object poses) or image observations; continuous end-effector actions
scale: 5 simulated tasks; 200 proficient-human demonstrations per task (PH), 300 multi-human demonstrations from 6 operators (MH), machine-generated sets for Lift and Can; 50 rollouts per evaluation
real_check: Three tasks (Lift, Can, Tool Hang) were also trained and evaluated on a real Franka arm with 200 demonstrations each; no sim-real correlation is reported.
status: Standard for single-task visuomotor policies (Diffusion Policy uses it); not a reporting target in the VLA papers checked. Both repositories maintained (pushed 2026-07 and 2026-08). No leaderboard
note: Robosuite (arXiv 2009.12293, v1.5 described in a 2025 revision) is the framework under LIBERO, RoboCasa and MimicGen. No VLA result on the robomimic tasks was found.

name: RoboCasa
evaluates: Everyday kitchen manipulation by a mobile manipulator: atomic skills (pick-and-place, doors, drawers, knobs, levers, buttons, navigation) and LLM-guided composite tasks across varied kitchens
improves: Earlier simulation suites lacked scene and object diversity and large demonstration sets for training and testing generalist policies
setup: Robosuite on MuJoCo; Franka Panda on a mobile base by default, other embodiments supported; three RGB cameras (eye-in-hand, left, right) plus proprioception; continuous arm, gripper and base actions
scale: 100 tasks (25 atomic, 75 composite); 120 kitchen scenes (10 floor plans x 12 styles); 2,509 objects in 153 categories; 50 human demonstrations per atomic task; 100K+ MimicGen trajectories (3,000 per task for 24 atomic tasks)
real_check: Sim-and-real co-training only: on a real Franka in a kitchen (3 pick-and-place tasks) success rose from 13.6% to 24.4% with simulation data; no sim-real correlation reported.
policies: GR00T N1 (32.1% at 100 demos), GR00T N1.5 (47.5% at 30 demos), GR00T N1.6 (66.2%), all on 24 atomic tasks; π0, π0.5 and SmolVLA via third-party runs; BC-Transformer and Diffusion Policy baselines
status: Standard target for GR00T-style models (24 atomic tasks, Panda); not saturated (highest 24-task averages found about 80%). Superseded by RoboCasa365, which holds the official leaderboard; repository pushed 2026-09
note: Released in 2024; included because VLA papers treat the 24-task protocol as established. Demo counts (30/100/300, human or generated) differ across papers; an audit found 53.3% of reported gains statistically significant (arXiv 2606.04233). Top scores from a third-party aggregate.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K
evaluates: Long-horizon household activities for mobile manipulators, defined by predicate-logic goal conditions over rigid, deformable and fluid objects
improves: Earlier embodied benchmarks chose tasks by designer convenience and lacked realistic physics; activities here come from a survey of what people want robots to do
setup: OmniGibson on NVIDIA Omniverse / PhysX 5; mobile manipulators (Tiago in the paper's real study; Galaxea R1 Pro for the released GR00T N1.6 checkpoint); RGB-D, proprioception and LiDAR; low-level control or action primitives
scale: 1,000 activities defined in BDDL, 50 scenes, 9,000+ objects in 1,900+ categories; survey of 1,461 participants
real_check: Preliminary sim-to-real study: a CollectTrash policy reached about 40% in simulation versus about 22% (oracle perception) and 0% (trained vision policy) on a real Tiago in a mock apartment.
policies: GR00T N1.6 (released BEHAVIOR-1K checkpoint; no score stated in its README)
status: Active through the 2025-2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge (catalogued separately); far from saturated; repository pushed 2026-09
note: The paper's baselines are RL with action primitives (visuomotor RL scored 0), not VLAs; VLA results come through the challenge task subset (see BEHAVIOR Challenge).

name: Franka Kitchen (Relay Policy Learning / D4RL kitchen)
evaluates: Multi-stage long-horizon manipulation: reaching a goal configuration of several kitchen fixtures (microwave, kettle, burners, light switch, cabinets) in one episode from unstructured demonstrations
improves: Imitation and reinforcement learning alone failed on long-horizon multi-stage tasks; the environment was built to test combining them from unstructured play data
setup: MuJoCo; 9-DoF Franka (arm plus gripper joints) with joint-velocity actions; 59-D state observations (image variants used by later work); sparse sub-task completion reward; 280-step episodes
scale: One kitchen scene; D4RL datasets from human demonstrations: complete (3,680 transitions), partial (136,950) and mixed (136,950)
status: Standard for behaviour-cloning and offline-RL policy papers (Diffusion Policy uses it); not a reporting target in the VLA papers checked. Maintained in Gymnasium-Robotics (pushed 2026-09)
note: No language conditioning and a single fixed scene. No VLA result on it was verified.

name: VIMA-Bench
evaluates: Tabletop manipulation specified by multimodal prompts (text interleaved with images or video frames), with four levels of zero-shot generalization from placement to novel tasks
improves: Task specifications (language, goal image, video demonstration) were handled by separate models and benchmarks; no suite tested them under one prompt format with graded generalization
setup: Ravens simulator on PyBullet; frontal and top-down RGB with object segmentation and boxes; pick-and-place and wipe primitives parameterized by end-effector poses
scale: 17 task templates in 6 categories, instantiated into thousands of procedurally generated tasks; 650K scripted expert trajectories (50K per task); 4 generalization levels (L1-L4)
status: Used mainly by multimodal-prompt policy papers (VIMA lineage); not a reporting target in the VLA papers checked. Repository last pushed 2023-09
note: High-level primitive actions rather than continuous control. No VLA result on it was verified.

name: ARNOLD
evaluates: Language-grounded manipulation toward continuous goal states (e.g., open a drawer halfway, pour half the water) in realistic 3D scenes, with splits for novel objects, scenes and goal states
improves: Earlier language-conditioned benchmarks used discrete binary goals and simple scenes, so they could not test grounding of continuous object states
setup: NVIDIA Isaac Sim with PhysX 5; 7-DoF Franka Panda with parallel gripper; five 128x128 RGB-D cameras; two-phase keyframe actions (grasp, then manipulate to the goal state)
scale: 8 tasks (PickupObject, ReorientObject, Open/CloseDrawer, Open/CloseCabinet, PourWater, TransferWater), 20 scenes, 40 objects, 10k demonstrations
real_check: A preliminary sim-to-real transfer on a real Franka (drawer and pickup tasks) is described, with the authors noting a remaining sim-to-real gap; no correlation reported.
status: Niche; baselines are PerAct-style models (about 55% on the test split, about 5% on novel goal states). Not a reporting target in the VLA papers checked. Repository last pushed 2025-03
note: No VLA result on it was verified; real-robot numbers were not extracted.

name: Language-Table (simulation)
evaluates: Open-vocabulary language following for planar block pushing, with a simulated multi-task benchmark alongside the real-robot dataset
improves: Earlier language-conditioned robot datasets were an order of magnitude smaller and did not support real-time language guidance
setup: PyBullet board with 8 blocks, modelled on the real setup (xArm6 with a cylindrical end-effector); RGB image observations; 2-D Cartesian delta actions
scale: 5 simulated task families spanning 696 task conditions (block-to-block, block-to-block-relative, block-to-absolute-location, block-to-relative-location, separate); 181,020 simulated and 442,226 real episodes
real_check: The same setup exists as a real robot and the paper's headline result (93.5% over 87,588 instructions) is real-robot; no sim-real correlation is reported.
status: Used by Google- and NVIDIA-lineage models and latent-action work; not a common target elsewhere. No leaderboard. Repository pushed 2026-09
note: Planar pushing only (2-D actions). The GR00T figures come from the N1.5 project page, which does not state the protocol.

name: ALOHA simulation tasks (ACT; gym-aloha)
evaluates: Fine-grained bimanual manipulation with joint-position control on two tasks: handing a cube between arms and inserting a peg into a socket in mid-air
improves: Introduced with ACT as simulated counterparts of the real ALOHA tasks, to compare imitation methods on precise bimanual control with scripted and human demonstrations
setup: MuJoCo; bimanual ALOHA with two ViperX arms; camera images plus joint positions; 14-D absolute joint-position actions (6 joints and a gripper per arm)
scale: 2 tasks (Transfer Cube, Bimanual Insertion); 50 demonstrations per task from a scripted policy or a human; ACT evaluated with 3 seeds x 50 rollouts
real_check: The ACT paper runs six separate real ALOHA tasks (80-90% success); the simulated tasks are not compared with real results.
policies: FLOWER (54.0% average); π0 via the openpi ALOHA-sim example (no score published there)
status: Small sanity-check benchmark supported by LeRobot and openpi; ACT reached 97% and 90% with scripted data, 82% and 60% with human data. No leaderboard. gym-aloha pushed 2026-09
note: Two tasks in one fixed scene and no language variation; rarely reported in VLA main tables.

name: Push-T
evaluates: Contact-rich planar pushing: moving a T-shaped block onto a fixed target pose with a circular end-effector, scored by target-area coverage
improves: Used in Diffusion Policy to test precise control under contact-rich dynamics and multimodal action distributions, which earlier behaviour-cloning benchmarks covered poorly
setup: 2-D pymunk physics with pygame rendering; state (agent and block pose), keypoint or 96x96 image observations; 2-D target-position actions
scale: 1 task; 200 human demonstrations in Diffusion Policy; solved when the block covers at least 95% of the goal zone
status: Single-task sanity check for imitation policies (Diffusion Policy 0.95 from state, 0.91 from images); supported by LeRobot; not a VLA reporting target. gym-pusht pushed 2026-09
note: No language and no 3-D manipulation. Whether Diffusion Policy's real-robot experiments include a Push-T counterpart was not checked, so real validation is left empty.

name: MimicGen
evaluates: Imitation learning from automatically generated demonstrations across tasks with varied initial-state distributions, objects and robot arms, including multi-part assembly and coffee preparation
improves: Collecting enough human demonstrations for broad initial-state coverage was costly; the system expands a few human demonstrations into large datasets
setup: Robosuite on MuJoCo and Factory tasks in Isaac Gym; Panda, Sawyer, IIWA and UR5e arms; low-dimensional or image observations; end-effector actions
scale: 18 tasks; over 50,000 generated demonstrations from about 200 human demonstrations
real_check: The data-generation system was also run on a real robot (Stack and Coffee tasks); no sim-real correlation is reported.
status: Data-generation system whose task set serves as a benchmark for imitation policies; underlies RoboCasa and DexMimicGen data. Not a reporting target in the VLA papers checked
note: Only the abstract and project page were opened; real-robot numbers and VLA usage were not verified.

name: RoboTwin 1.0
venue: CVPR 2025 (Highlight); early version at ECCV 2024 workshop
evaluates: Dual-arm coordination on tabletop tool-use and pick-and-place tasks, with expert data produced by LLM-generated code over generative digital twins of objects
improves: Lack of standardized dual-arm benchmarks and of scalable expert data for bimanual tasks aligned with a real dual-arm platform
setup: SAPIEN-based simulation (the arXiv HTML names ManiSkill3); AgileX COBOT Magic dual-arm platform with four RealSense D435 RGB-D cameras; image or point-cloud observations
scale: 15 tasks (two with easy/hard variants); policies trained with 20, 50 or 100 generated expert demonstrations per task
real_check: Sim-to-real transfer only: policies pretrained on 300 simulated samples and fine-tuned on 20 real samples on a COBOT Magic improved over real-only training (about 70% single-arm, 40% dual-arm); no sim-real correlation reported.
status: Superseded by RoboTwin 2.0; basis of the CVPR 2025 MEIS dual-arm collaboration challenge. No separate leaderboard
note: Paper baselines are Diffusion Policy and DP3 only. Year refers to the early arXiv version (2409.02920), which was not opened; details come from arXiv 2504.13059.

name: RoboTwin 2.0
evaluates: Bimanual tabletop manipulation across 50 tasks, reported separately for clean scenes and scenes randomized in clutter, lighting, background, table height and language
improves: Earlier bimanual simulation suites had few tasks, one embodiment and little visual or language variation, so policies overfit to clean scenes
setup: SAPIEN; five dual-arm embodiments (Aloha-AgileX, ARX-X5, Piper, Franka, UR5); leaderboard protocol uses Aloha-AgileX with head and two wrist RGB cameras and 14-D joint actions
scale: 50 tasks; 731 objects in 147 categories (RoboTwin-OD); 100,000+ expert trajectories; 50 clean demos per task for training and 100 evaluation episodes per task per setting (Easy/Hard)
real_check: Sim-to-real transfer only: on a COBOT-Magic robot (4 tasks), adding 1,000 randomized synthetic trajectories to 10 real demos, or training on synthetic data alone, raised real success; no sim-real policy-ranking correlation reported.
policies: π0, RDT (paper); π0.5, X-VLA, GR00T N1.6, OpenVLA-OFT, InternVLA-A1, StarVLA-α, FastWAM, Spatial Forcing, X-WAM (later papers and XPolicyLab)
status: Widely adopted outside the originating lab (LeRobot, StarVLA, vla-eval, XPolicyLab with 42 integrated policies). Leaderboard: https://robotwin-platform.github.io/leaderboard
note: Two training protocols circulate (50 clean demos per task vs. 50 clean + 500 randomized demos per task), so scores across papers are not directly comparable. The leaderboard table did not render when fetched.

name: RoboCasa365
evaluates: Multi-task household mobile manipulation in kitchens: atomic skills, seen composite tasks and unseen composite tasks, under multi-task, foundation-model fine-tuning and lifelong-learning protocols
improves: Original RoboCasa had about 100 tasks and 120 scenes with a small evaluated subset; larger task and scene diversity was needed to study generalist training at scale
setup: MuJoCo (robosuite/RoboCasa); Franka Panda on an Omron mobile base; three 256x256 RGB cameras plus proprioception; 12-D actions (arm end-effector, gripper, base and torso)
scale: 365 tasks (65 atomic, 300 composite); 2,500 kitchen scenes; 600+ h human and 1,600+ h MimicGen-generated demonstrations; leaderboard evaluates 50 tasks (18 atomic, 16 composite-seen, 16 composite-unseen)
real_check: Sim-and-real co-training only: on a DROID-style Franka in a real kitchen (4 tasks, 20 trials each), co-training with simulation data reached 79.8% vs 61.8% for real-only; no sim-real correlation reported.
policies: π0, π0.5, GR00T N1.5, GR00T N1.6, Xiaomi-Robotics-1, ABot-M0.5/M0.6, RLDX-1, PRTS, GigaWorld-Policy 0.1, Paimon-0, Phasor-m7, WorldDreamer
status: Growing adoption: 15 leaderboard entries by 2026-09, most from outside the originating lab. Leaderboard: https://robocasa.ai/leaderboard.html
note: Baseline numbers on the leaderboard (e.g. GR00T N1.5 23.9 average) differ from the values extracted from the arXiv paper (20.0); the leaderboard appears to carry updated runs.

name: RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop Tasks
venue: arXiv 2025-03 (introduced in the GR00T N1 paper)
evaluates: Language-conditioned tabletop rearrangement and articulated-object tasks performed by a humanoid upper body with dexterous hands from an egocentric camera
improves: No simulated counterpart existed for real humanoid tabletop data, so humanoid foundation models could not be compared reproducibly in simulation
setup: MuJoCo via RoboCasa/robosuite; Fourier GR-1 humanoid with Fourier dexterous hands; egocentric head camera; joint-space actions for arms, hands, waist and neck
scale: 24 tasks (18 pick-and-place rearrangement, 6 articulated-object); 1,000 demonstrations per task; a 240k-trajectory tabletop dataset is also released
policies: GR00T N1, N1.5, N1.6, N1.7; StarVLA-α; TwinBrainVLA; π0, π0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT as baselines in third-party papers
status: Common humanoid row in 2026 VLA result tables (StarVLA-α, TwinBrainVLA, ABot-M0, VP-VLA, DIAL). No official leaderboard found
note: The GR00T N1 paper describes the suite as a digital counterpart to real humanoid data but reports no paired sim-real evaluation. The repo README could only be read via the raw file.

name: DexMimicGen
evaluates: Bimanual manipulation with grippers and dexterous hands (assembly, threading, transport, pouring, packing, sorting) learned from automatically generated demonstrations
improves: MimicGen-style data generation and its task suites covered only single-arm gripper robots, leaving bimanual dexterous and humanoid setups without scalable data or benchmarks
setup: MuJoCo via robosuite; three embodiments: bimanual Panda with parallel grippers, bimanual Panda with dexterous hands, GR-1 humanoid with dexterous hands
scale: 9 tasks (3 per embodiment); 21K generated demonstrations from 60 human demonstrations
real_check: Real-to-sim-to-real transfer only: a can-sorting policy for a real GR-1 trained on generated data reached 90% vs 0% with source demos alone; no sim-real correlation reported.
policies: GR00T N1 (the 9-task set is the 'DexMimicGen Cross-Embodiment Suite' in the GR00T N1 paper)
status: Used mainly by NVIDIA GEAR-affiliated work as a cross-embodiment benchmark. No leaderboard
note: Paper baselines are BC-RNN and Diffusion Policy; the GR00T N1 result (66.5% at 100 demos per task) comes from the GR00T N1 paper.

name: RoboVerse
evaluates: Imitation and reinforcement learning policies on tasks unified from many existing suites, at four generalization levels (task space, environment, camera, lighting and reflection)
improves: Fragmentation across simulators and benchmarks, which prevents shared data formats, cross-simulator evaluation and consistent protocols
setup: MetaSim layer over Isaac Sim/Lab, Isaac Gym, MuJoCo, SAPIEN, PyBullet and Genesis (CoppeliaSim via PyRep per README); multiple arms, hands and humanoids; unified Gym-style interface
scale: About 1,000 tasks (276 manipulation task categories), about 500k trajectories, about 5.5k assets
real_check: Sim-to-real transfer only: the paper reports direct sim-to-real transfer of imitation policies and sim-to-sim-to-real transfer of RL policies; no sim-real correlation reported.
status: Used as infrastructure rather than as a standard results table; no leaderboard found
note: Baseline names and real-robot numbers could not be extracted from the arXiv HTML; VLA baselines in the paper are therefore unverified.

name: PerAct2 / RLBench2
evaluates: Language-conditioned bimanual 6-DoF manipulation requiring spatial and temporal coordination of two arms
improves: RLBench had no bimanual tasks, and no simulated benchmark existed for language-conditioned two-arm manipulation
setup: Extension of RLBench to two arms; language-conditioned 6-DoF bimanual actions (robot model and camera setup not captured)
scale: 13 tasks with 23 variations
real_check: The project page states the method also runs on a real robot, with minimal detail; no sim-real correlation reported.
status: Used by later 3D bimanual policy papers (e.g. AnyBimanual); less common in VLA result tables. No leaderboard
note: A search summary describes it as a CoRL 2024 workshop paper, but neither arXiv nor the repo README states a venue. Robot model and demo counts were not captured.

name: BiGym
evaluates: Mobile bimanual manipulation by a humanoid in home scenes, from reaching to kitchen cleaning, learned from human-collected demonstrations
improves: Existing benchmarks relied on planner-generated demonstrations and fixed-base arms; human-teleoperated, multimodal demonstrations for mobile bimanual tasks were missing
setup: MuJoCo; Unitree H1 with two Robotiq 2F-85 grippers; proprioception plus RGB-D from head and two wrist cameras; whole-body (23-D) or bimanual floating-base (16-D) action modes
scale: 40 tasks; 50 VR-teleoperated human demonstrations per task
status: Limited adoption in VLA papers; baselines are ACT, Diffusion Policy, BC and demo-driven RL. No leaderboard
note: Venue taken from the CoRL 2024 proceedings listing; the arXiv page lists no venue.

name: HumanoidBench
evaluates: Whole-body humanoid control with dexterous hands on locomotion tasks and manipulation tasks such as shelf rearrangement, package unloading and window wiping
improves: Humanoid learning research lacked a shared simulated benchmark combining locomotion with dexterous whole-body manipulation
setup: MuJoCo; Unitree H1 with two Shadow Hands (Digit and gripper variants supported); proprioceptive, egocentric visual and tactile observations
scale: 27 tasks (15 whole-body manipulation, 12 locomotion)
status: Adopted mainly as a reinforcement-learning benchmark; no VLA results found. No leaderboard
note: Reward-based RL benchmark without demonstrations. The manipulation/locomotion split comes from the RSS 2024 paper listing.

name: ManiSkill-HAB
evaluates: Low-level whole-body control for long-horizon home rearrangement (TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable), decomposed into Pick, Place, Open and Close subtasks
improves: Home Assistant Benchmark implementations were slow and used magical grasping; realistic contact and fast GPU simulation were needed for low-level manipulation research
setup: GPU-parallel ManiSkill3 (SAPIEN) port of the Home Assistant Benchmark; mobile manipulator with whole-body control (robot model not captured)
scale: 3 long-horizon tasks; released datasets of 18K, 18K and 8K episodes (8.8M transitions) generated by RL policies with rule-based filtering
status: Used for RL and IL research on mobile manipulation; no VLA results found. No leaderboard
note: Robot model was not captured. Baselines in the paper are RL and imitation-learning policies that do not solve the tasks.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge
evaluates: Full-length household activities requiring navigation, bimanual manipulation and long-horizon sequencing, scored by partial credit over BDDL goal predicates
improves: BEHAVIOR-1K had no demonstration data or standardized learning protocol; the challenge adds teleoperated demonstrations, baselines and a held-out evaluation
setup: OmniGibson on Isaac Sim; mobile-base bimanual robot with two 7-DoF arms and parallel grippers; RGB, depth and proprioception (2025 also had a privileged-information track)
scale: 2025: 50 tasks, 10,000 teleoperated demonstrations (1,200+ h). 2026: 100 tasks, 20,000 demonstrations (1,950 h), 7 scenes
policies: π0.5-based entries placed 1st (q-score 0.2599) and 2nd (0.2514) in 2025; organizer baselines include OpenVLA and π0 (2025), π0.5 and GR00T N1.7 (2026)
status: Active competition; 2025 results announced at NeurIPS 2025, 2026 submissions close 2026-10-16. Leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/behavior-1k/2026-challenge-leaderboard
note: No organizer report paper was found; 2025 scores come from the 1st-place solution report (arXiv 2512.06951). The robot name was not stated on the pages opened.

name: RoboDojo simulation suite
evaluates: Bimanual policies along five capability dimensions: generalization, memory, long-horizon execution, precision and open (unseen task specifications)
improves: Existing simulation suites were close to saturated and reported one success number; a harder, capability-structured suite paired with a real-robot counterpart was missing
setup: Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab with heterogeneous parallel simulation; ARX X5 bimanual platform; policies connected through XPolicyLab
scale: 42 tasks (12 generalization, 6 memory, 8 long-horizon, 8 precision, 8 open); 3,500 training trajectories (20.66 h); 50 evaluation episodes per task
real_check: Paired with 18 real-world tasks on three bimanual platforms (RoboDojo-RealEval); the paper reports partial but not complete agreement between simulation and real leaderboards, without a correlation coefficient in the text captured.
policies: 30 policies including π0, π0.5, X-VLA, GR00T N1.7, OpenVLA-OFT, RDT-1B, H-RDT, SmolVLA, InternVLA-A1, GO-1, MolmoAct2, Xiaomi-Robotics-0, StarVLA-α, Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA
status: New; best policy reaches 8.80% average success against 76.03% for human teleoperation. Leaderboard: https://robodojo-benchmark.com/leaderboard
note: The real-robot half (RoboDojo-RealEval) is already catalogued separately. Scores are from the paper; the leaderboard page was not opened.

name: EBench
evaluates: Generalist mobile manipulation policies profiled by scene, atomic skill, horizon, precision and operating mode, and by generalization to unseen backgrounds, objects, instructions and their combination
improves: A single overall success rate hides which capabilities a policy has and where it overfits to training assets
setup: Isaac Sim (60 Hz); dual-arm robot on a mobile base; three 224x224 RGB views plus proprioception and language; per-arm joint or end-effector actions plus base velocity
scale: 26 tasks (10 mobile pick-and-place, 9 mobile long-horizon, 7 tabletop dexterous/precise) in 9 scene categories; 6,600 demonstration episodes (91.4 h); 510 test episodes
policies: π0 (34.4% test success), π0.5 (41.0%), X-VLA (24.7%), InternVLA-A1 (27.6%)
status: New; hosted leaderboard at https://internrobotics.shlab.org.cn/eval/evaluation-list. Adoption outside the originating lab not verified
note: Authors state they do not claim simulation scores predict real-robot performance. Scores are from arXiv v3 as extracted.

name: RoboEval
evaluates: Bimanual manipulation with behavioral metrics for efficiency, coordination and safety/stability, plus stage-wise progress, alongside binary success
improves: Binary success hides failure modes such as poor coordination, object slip and asymmetric arm use
setup: MuJoCo; bimanual Franka Panda with parallel grippers; proprioceptive and visual observations; joint-position or end-effector-delta actions
scale: 8 base tasks with 28 variations (static, position, rotation, position+rotation); 3,000+ human VR demonstrations
policies: GR00T N1.6, X-VLA, π0.5 (v2 of the paper), alongside ACT and Diffusion Policy
status: Early adoption; code repo marked 'In Submission'; leaderboard section on the project page https://robo-eval.github.io
note: The project page mentions a CoRL 2026 workshop, which may be a presentation rather than the publication venue. Per-policy numbers were only captured as ranges.

name: SIMPLE
evaluates: Humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with dexterous hands in indoor scenes, at three domain-randomization levels
improves: Humanoid VLA evaluation lacked a simulator combining reliable contact physics for locomotion with photorealistic rendering and many whole-body tasks
setup: MuJoCo physics coupled with Isaac Sim rendering; Unitree G1 with dexterous hands; 32-D proprioceptive state and 36-D actions (upper-body targets plus locomotion commands)
scale: 60 tasks, 50 indoor scenes, 1,000+ object assets; 6,000+ episodes rendered for benchmarking (project page states 100,000+ demonstrations)
real_check: Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on two tasks (pick-and-place 90% sim vs 80% real; handover 100% vs 80%); the authors claim strong sim-real agreement from this limited test, without a correlation statistic.
policies: Ψ0, π0.5, GR00T N1.6, InternVLA, H-RDT, EgoVLA, DreamZero, plus Diffusion Policy and ACT
status: New; project page mentions a hosted leaderboard. Adoption outside the originating lab not verified
note: A search result associates the paper with CoRL 2026, not confirmed on arXiv or the project page. Demonstration counts differ between paper and project page.

name: MobileManiBench
evaluates: VLA policies for mobile manipulation of articulated and rigid objects (open, close, pull, push, pick) on unseen objects and unseen scenes
improves: VLA architectures were verified mainly on fixed-base tabletop data; a simulation-first testbed for mobile bases and dexterous hands was missing
setup: Isaac Sim; two mobile robots (AgiBot G1 with parallel gripper, XHand robot with 12-DoF dexterous hand); head and wrist RGB-D; 6-D wrist pose delta plus end-effector joints
scale: 630 objects in 20 categories, 5 skills, 100+ tasks, 100 scenes, 300K trajectories generated by RL policies
policies: OpenVLA (4.5%), CogACT (6.8%), π0 (11.2%), π0.5 (18.8%), MobileManiVLA (28.2%)
status: New; code and dataset released. Adoption outside the originating lab not verified. No leaderboard
note: The arXiv text refers to real-robot results in an appendix, but none were visible in the HTML or on the project page; treated as simulation only.

name: DexVerse
evaluates: Multi-task, multi-embodiment dexterous-hand manipulation: grasping, functional tool use, articulated objects, non-prehensile and contact-rich skills, bimanual and long-horizon tasks
improves: Dexterous benchmarks covered isolated tasks and single hands, preventing systematic comparison across interaction modes, sensing conditions and embodiments
setup: Isaac Lab; 3 arms (Franka Research 3, UR10e, xArm 7) and 6 hands (Sharpa Wave, WUJI, Shadow, Inspire, Allegro, LEAP); proprioception, RGB, depth, point cloud, contact forces; absolute joint targets
scale: 100 tasks in 8 categories; 3,180 teleoperated demonstrations; baselines run on 19 tasks with 50 episodes per task
policies: π0.5 (34%), OpenVLA (19%), alongside DP3 (34%) and Diffusion Policy (32%)
status: New; no adoption outside the originating lab verified. No leaderboard
note: Baselines cover 19 of the 100 tasks. A code repository link was not found on the pages opened.

name: DexJoCo
evaluates: Task-oriented dexterous-hand manipulation: tool use, bimanual coordination, long-horizon execution and reasoning tasks such as Hanoi and unlocking a tablet
improves: Dexterous benchmarks focused on grasping or in-hand reorientation rather than functional tasks, and lacked low-cost demonstration tooling on MuJoCo
setup: MuJoCo; Franka Panda arm(s) with Allegro Hand; visual, placement and dynamics domain randomization; glove-and-tracker teleoperation toolkit
scale: 11 tasks; 1.1K teleoperated trajectories (100 per task)
policies: π0.5 (40.2%), GR00T N1.5 (40.2%), alongside ACT (54.1%) and Diffusion Policy (47.6-50.4%)
status: New; no adoption outside the originating lab verified. No leaderboard
note: Success rates are for the randomized-object condition as extracted from arXiv v2.

name: BiCoord
evaluates: Long-horizon bimanual tasks with tight spatial-temporal coupling between arms, measured with stage-wise success and coordination metrics
improves: Existing bimanual suites contain many tasks where the arms act independently or sequentially over short horizons
setup: Built on RoboTwin 2.0 (SAPIEN); dual-arm robot with end-effector pose and gripper control
scale: 18 tasks; 100 trajectories per task (1,800 total)
policies: π0 (46.4%), OpenVLA-OFT (40.5%), RDT (39.5%), alongside Diffusion Policy (33.1%)
status: New; no adoption outside the originating lab verified. No leaderboard
note: The π0 figure coincides with RoboTwin 2.0's reported π0 Easy score and should be re-checked against the paper table.

name: LBM Eval
evaluates: Multitask language-conditioned bimanual manipulation by large behavior models on seen and unseen tasks, with statistical testing over many rollouts
improves: Multitask policy comparisons often lacked enough rollouts and statistical analysis to support conclusions about pretraining
setup: Drake; bimanual station with two Franka FR3 arms and parallel grippers; policies connect through a gRPC wrapper
scale: 49 tasks in the open-source release across four scenarios; the paper evaluates 16 seen and 8 unseen simulated tasks with 200 rollouts per task per policy
real_check: Three seen tasks were evaluated in both simulation and the real world; the authors note discrepancies and do not report a systematic sim-real correlation.
policies: TRI LBM (diffusion transformer); Foundry-VLA-1.7B and Foundry-Qwen3VLA-2.1B (VLA Foundry)
status: Open source (124 GitHub stars) but results found only from Toyota Research Institute. No leaderboard
note: Scenario task counts in the paper sum to 48 while the repo states 49. No third-party results were found.

name: GenManip-Bench
evaluates: Instruction-following tabletop manipulation requiring spatial, appearance, common-sense and long-horizon reasoning, comparing modular foundation-model systems with end-to-end policies
improves: Simulation platforms offered limited instruction and scenario diversity for studying policy generalization
setup: Isaac Sim; single Franka arm on a tabletop; LLM-driven task-oriented scene-graph generation over about 10K annotated 3D assets
scale: 200 human-refined benchmark scenarios (a CVPR listing states 250)
policies: GR-1 and ACT as end-to-end policies; CoPA and MOKA as modular systems; later included in the InternManip suite alongside GR00T N1/N1.5 and π0
status: Used mainly within InternRobotics (Shanghai AI Lab) tooling; no leaderboard found
note: Scenario count differs between the arXiv abstract (200) and a conference listing seen in search results (250).

name: RoboFactory
evaluates: Multi-arm collaborative manipulation with one to four agents under logical, spatial and temporal compositional constraints
improves: Embodied multi-agent manipulation lacked benchmarks and automated data collection that enforce safe and efficient collaboration
setup: ManiSkill (SAPIEN); one to four Franka Panda arms; RGB observations and joint actions
scale: 11 tasks (3 one-agent, 4 two-agent, 2 three-agent, 2 four-agent); 150 demonstrations per task
status: Limited adoption; baseline is Diffusion Policy (49% one-agent to 10% four-agent average). No leaderboard
note: Venue taken from the repository title and CVF open-access listing seen in search results.

name: HumanoidGen
evaluates: Bimanual dexterous manipulation by a humanoid with five-finger hands on tasks created and solved through LLM-planned spatial constraints
improves: Simulation tasks and demonstrations existed mostly for gripper arms; humanoids with dual arms and dexterous hands lacked both
setup: SAPIEN; Unitree H1-2 with Inspire hands (26-D action space); RGB-D from six camera views
scale: 20 tasks; 100 generated demonstrations per task
real_check: The paper reports real-robot experiments in an appendix; details were not captured and no sim-real correlation is reported in the main text.
status: Limited adoption; baselines are Diffusion Policy and DP3. No leaderboard
note: An OpenReview copy exists, but the venue was not confirmed.

name: AgentWorld
evaluates: Household mobile manipulation on basic skills and multistage living-room, kitchen and bedroom tasks in procedurally constructed scenes
improves: Scene construction and mobile teleoperated data collection for household tasks were not available in one platform
setup: Isaac Sim (PhysX 5); Unitree G1 and H1, Franka Panda on a wheeled base, DOBOT X-Trainer; parallel gripper or dexterous hand
scale: 150 procedurally generated household scenes, 9,000+ assets, 1,000+ teleoperated trajectories; 3 basic and 9 multistage task types
real_check: Sim-and-real co-training only: 100 simulated plus 9 real demonstrations gave 29.3% real success on pick-and-place; no sim-real correlation reported.
policies: π0 (64-82% basic, 18-30% multistage), alongside BC, ACT and Diffusion Policy
status: Limited adoption outside the originating lab. No leaderboard
note: Success ranges are as extracted from arXiv v2.

name: RoboBenchMart
evaluates: Mobile manipulation of grocery items in dark-store retail scenes with dense shelves and fridges, on seen and unseen scenes and items
improves: Manipulation benchmarks centre on tabletop and household scenes; cluttered multi-level retail shelves were not covered
setup: ManiSkill3; Fetch mobile manipulator (differential-drive base, 7-DoF arm, torso, parallel gripper); procedurally generated store layouts
scale: 5 atomic and 2 composite tasks; 370 product assets in 21 categories; 2,976 motion-planned trajectories
policies: Octo, SmolVLA, π0, π0.5 (best: π0.5 55% in-domain on pick-to-basket; all models 0% on composite tasks)
status: Limited adoption. No leaderboard
note: Per-task numbers are as extracted from arXiv v2.

name: AutoBio
evaluates: Language-guided manipulation of biology-lab instruments (tube caps, thermal cyclers, mixers) at three difficulty levels requiring precision, visual reasoning and protocol following
improves: General simulators lacked lab instruments, threaded and detent mechanisms, liquids, transparent materials and dynamic instrument displays
setup: MuJoCo with custom physics plugins and optional Blender rendering; ALOHA and UR5e (Robotiq gripper or dexterous hand)
scale: 16 tasks across 3 difficulty levels; 100 demonstrations per task
policies: π0 and RDT (about 83-86% on easy tasks, 1-21% on medium, 4-8% on hard)
status: Domain-specific; cited by later lab-automation benchmarks. No leaderboard
note: ICLR 2026 venue comes from an ICLR proceedings listing seen in search results, not from the arXiv page.

name: LabUtopia
evaluates: Scientific-lab manipulation at hierarchical levels from atomic actions through combined and generalization tasks to long-horizon mobile manipulation
improves: Embodied benchmarks lacked chemistry-lab scenes, multi-physics (liquids, heating) and a task hierarchy for scientific procedures
setup: Isaac Sim; Franka arm (mobile robot for navigation tasks); procedurally generated laboratory scenes
scale: 24 tasks across 4 levels per the repository README (10 basic, 6 combined, 6 generalization, 2 long-sequence)
status: Domain-specific; baselines are ACT and Diffusion Policy. No leaderboard
note: Task and level counts come from the repository README; the paper itself was not opened and may state different totals.

name: Labimus
evaluates: Humanoid dexterous manipulation in a chemistry lab, including powder scooping and weighing checked against quantitative tolerances from instrument readouts
improves: Lab benchmarks scored task completion only and lacked powder physics and closed-loop instrument feedback for protocol-level accuracy
setup: Isaac Sim (PhysX, particle-based powder); Tianyi 2.0 humanoid upper body with BrainCo Revo 2 dexterous hands
scale: 7 tasks (6 atomic operations and one seven-step solid-weighing workflow); 100 teleoperated demonstrations per task; 30+ lab assets
policies: π0, alongside ACT and Diffusion Policy
status: New, domain-specific. No leaderboard
note: Authors state all experiments are in simulation and real-world validation is planned.

name: Pipette
evaluates: Wet-lab manipulation covering sample and culture-ware handling, equipment hatch control and instrument placement, with and without simulation data augmentation
improves: Wet-lab robot learning lacked open editable lab assets, customizable simulation and pipelines that expand a few demonstrations into training data
setup: Isaac Sim 5.1 / Isaac Lab 2.3; three arm embodiments including Franka Panda and an AgileX arm
scale: 12 tasks; 100+ wet-lab assets; 30 human demonstrations per task as the base data budget
policies: π0, SmolVLA, alongside ACT
status: New, domain-specific. No leaderboard
note: Success rates were not captured; the third embodiment was not named in the text extracted.

name: Assemble Bench
evaluates: Contact-rich assembly by VLA and world-action models: round and square peg insertion, gear meshing and nut threading at several sizes
improves: VLA simulation benchmarks rarely include tight-clearance assembly, and lacked a training and evaluation loop for it on a common platform
setup: Isaac Lab-Arena; DROID platform (7-DoF Franka arm with Robotiq gripper); tasks modelled on NIST Assembly Task Boards
scale: 14 tasks in 4 suites (4 round peg, 4 square peg, 3 gear, 3 nut); 1,355 scripted-expert demonstrations
real_check: One real-robot video of a 4 mm round-peg insertion with π0.5 is shown; no systematic real evaluation or sim-real correlation.
policies: π0.5 (DROID-finetuned; behavior cloning and CG-DAgger variants)
status: New; released by a company (HUD) without a paper. No leaderboard found
note: No arXiv paper; all details come from the HUD blog page.

name: Isaac Lab-Arena task suites
evaluates: Generalist policies on GPU-parallel re-implementations of RoboCasa and LIBERO tasks, composed from separate object, scene, embodiment and task blocks
improves: Benchmark authoring in simulation was slow and suites were tied to one simulator; large-scale parallel evaluation of one policy across many environments was hard
setup: Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim; GR1 humanoid and Franka arm; integrated with the LeRobot Environment Hub
scale: 250+ tasks across the Lightwheel-RoboCasa-Tasks and Lightwheel-LIBERO-Tasks suites
policies: GR00T N1.5, π0 and SmolVLA are listed as supported policies; no result table was found
status: Framework used by later suites (X2Real, RoboFinals, Assemble Bench). No leaderboard
note: A framework rather than a single benchmark; no published scores were found. Year is the date of the blog post opened; an earlier pre-release may exist.

name: RoboFinals-100
evaluates: Frontier robot foundation models on household, factory and retail tasks with rigid, articulated and deformable objects at graded difficulty
improves: Developers report that academic simulation benchmarks are saturated by frontier models, pushing evaluation back to slow real-world testing
setup: Isaac Lab-Arena with Newton or PhysX physics, also MuJoCo and Genesis; tabletop arms, mobile manipulators and loco-manipulation robots
scale: 100 tasks
real_check: The vendor states that assets are Real2Sim-calibrated; no real-robot evaluation or sim-real correlation is published.
status: Commercial and not publicly released; Qwen is the only named user. No public leaderboard
note: All information comes from the vendor's product page; no paper and no public results.

name: GarmentLab
evaluates: Garment and deformable-object manipulation involving interactions among garments, rigid bodies, fluids and human bodies
improves: Garment manipulation lacked a unified simulation with diverse garment types, multiple physics methods and sim-to-real support
setup: Simulation combining FEM and PBD methods with multiple robots and manipulators (simulator name not captured)
scale: 20 tasks in 5 groups
real_check: The abstract describes sim-to-real algorithms and a real-world benchmark; no sim-real correlation was captured.
status: Used in garment-manipulation research; no VLA results found. No leaderboard
note: Only the arXiv abstract page was opened; the task count comes from a search snippet of the NeurIPS paper.

name: DexGarmentLab
evaluates: Bimanual dexterous-hand garment manipulation and generalization to unseen garment shapes and deformations
improves: Garment simulation environments targeted grippers; dexterous bimanual garment tasks lacked an environment and automatic data collection
setup: Garment simulation with dexterous hands (simulator name not captured)
scale: 15 task scenarios; trajectories generated from a single demonstration per task
status: Domain-specific; no VLA results found. No leaderboard
note: Only the arXiv abstract page was opened; real-robot content, simulator and baselines were not verified.

name: DOMINO
evaluates: Manipulation of moving objects (interception and tracking) under three levels of motion complexity, scored by success rate and a continuous manipulation score
improves: Earlier simulation benchmarks assume a static world in which only the robot changes the state, and dynamic manipulation data for training VLAs was scarce
setup: SAPIEN; built on RoboTwin 2.0; five embodiments (Aloha-AgileX, Franka Panda, Piper, UR5-WSG, ARX-X5), main experiments on Aloha-AgileX
scale: 35 tasks; 110K+ expert trajectories; 3 dynamics levels (constant velocity, polynomial, multi-segment with abrupt transitions); speed coefficient alpha
real_check: ACT, RDT-1B, π0.5 and PUMA were fine-tuned with 50 teleoperated demos per task and tested on 5 DOMINO tasks (20 trials each) on an AgileX Piper (averages 7%, 8%, 24%, 42%); method transfer only, no sim-real correlation reported.
policies: ACT, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, RDT-1B, π0, π0.5, InternVLA-M1, PUMA; static-trained policies drop below 8% success on dynamic tasks, dynamic fine-tuning adds under 3 points, PUMA reaches 17.2% SR
status: Code, dataset and PUMA weights released; no leaderboard; extended by DOMINO-Long (D2-VLA), used in the DSDyn-VLA appendix, cited as prior work by MotionForge; PUMA is a baseline in ReflexBench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment and project page. The paper's stated 6.3-point gain over baselines could not be reconciled with the extracted table.

name: DOM (DynamicVLA)
