evaluates: Manipulation of objects in motion along nine sub-dimensions of interaction, perception and generalization, including closed-loop reactivity and disturbance robustness
improves: Robot datasets are mostly static and teleoperation cannot track fast objects; inference latency makes actions stale by execution time
setup: Isaac Sim with an automatic demonstrator driven by object pose and velocity; 3D-FRONT scenes and Objaverse objects; Franka Emika Panda and AgileX PiPER
scale: 200K synthetic episodes; 2.8K scenes; 206 objects; 2K real episodes; 3 dimensions x 3 sub-dimensions
real_check: The benchmark has its own real-robot arm: 16 real tasks on Franka and PiPER, 60 trials per task (960 trials per method); no sim-real correlation statistic is reported.
policies: Diffusion Policy, ACT, OpenVLA-OFT, π0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T-N1.5, RTC, VLA-Adapter-Pro, VLASH, DynamicVLA; DynamicVLA 47.06% average success vs 12.33% for the best baseline (VLASH)
status: Project page available; DynamicVLA is a baseline in ReflexBench and DynBench, and DOM is cited as prior work by MotionForge; no leaderboard found
note: Venue is the arXiv comment field ('NeurIPS 2026'); not checked against the NeurIPS site.

name: DOMINO-Long
evaluates: Retaining cues seen early in an episode (object locations, presentation order, colour instructions) while manipulating moving objects over several stages
improves: Original DOMINO tasks are short-horizon and place weak demands on long-term memory
setup: RoboTwin 2.0 / DOMINO; Aloha-AgileX bimanual robot
scale: 10 multi-stage tasks; 50 demonstrations per task (500 total, 227,208 records); episodes of 201-911 steps
real_check: The proposed D2-VLA was compared with π0.5 and MemoryVLA on eight long-horizon tasks (four static, four dynamic) on a Unitree G1D; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: PUMA 20.6%, π0.5 35.4%, D2-VLA 60.0% success
status: Introduced inside a method paper (D2-VLA); code repository and project page listed; no independent adoption seen
note: Physics engine not stated in the extracted text; inherited from DOMINO.

name: MotionForge
evaluates: Long-horizon manipulation of moving objects under factorized domain shifts (object, background, lighting, motion speed) with latency-aware real-time execution
improves: Existing dynamic benchmarks do not jointly cover diverse motion patterns, long horizons, systematic domain shift and latency-aware evaluation
setup: Isaac Sim; positions itself against DOM, DOMINO and PhysMani-Bench; robot embodiment not stated in the extracted text
scale: 40 tasks in 4 scene families (17 long-horizon); 11 motion patterns; about 20,000 demonstration episodes; 4 shift axes plus joint shift
policies: Diffusion Policy, ACT, SmolVLA, X-VLA, π0.5, GR00T N1.7, FastWAM; best in-domain result is ACT at 22.2%, best under joint shift 5.85%; freezing the scene adds 21.7-27.5 points
status: New preprint; no code or project URL found

name: ReflexBench
evaluates: Reaction-critical manipulation where inference latency separates perception from execution: conveyor pick-and-place, ball catching, interception, throwing, rotating-peg insertion
improves: Existing dynamic benchmarks evaluate only and do not provide a common framework for studying anticipation together with inference efficiency
setup: Simulation with a real-time-factor metric; simulator and simulated robot not stated in the extracted text; real robot is an AgileX Piper
scale: 6 tasks; 200 demonstrations per task
real_check: Three tasks (conveyor pick-and-place, button pressing, ball catching) were run on an AgileX Piper with ReflexVLA, PUMA and SmolVLA, 20 runs per task; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: ReflexVLA 50.4%, PUMA 50.2%, SmolVLA 38.3%, DynamicVLA 37.3%, π0.5 36.9%, OpenVLA-OFT 36.0%, VLA-Adapter 30.3%
status: Introduced inside a method paper (Reflex); project page listed; no independent adoption seen
note: Simulator name could not be confirmed.

name: DynBench
evaluates: Vision-based manipulation of moving objects: conveyor picking and sorting, dropping and stacking onto moving targets, insertion into a moving hole, grasping rolling objects
improves: The state-based Kinetix benchmark does not exercise the visual pipeline of a VLA in dynamic scenes
setup: MuJoCo; Franka Panda; four real dynamic tasks ported to simulation and expanded
scale: 9 tasks; 100 rule-generated demonstrations per task
real_check: Four tasks (conveyor picking, dynamic dropping, dynamic stacking, mobile pouring) were run on an AgileX Piper, 50 trials each; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: π0.5 9.7%, RTC 19.4%, VLASH 27.1%, DynamicVLA 34.3%, DSDyn-VLA 48.4% average success
status: Introduced inside a method paper (DSDyn-VLA); code promised but no URL found

name: PhysMani-Bench
evaluates: Manipulation of fast-moving targets (moving belts, rotating racks) at normal and high speed in 3D scenes
improves: Benchmarks focus on static or quasi-static manipulation and dynamic-target manipulation is little studied
setup: Extended from RLBench; Franka Emika Panda in simulation; Astribot S1 for real tests
scale: 16 tasks (8 groups x 2 speeds); 160 trajectories per task (2,560 total)
real_check: Four dynamic tasks on an Astribot S1 (64 trials per task) compared PhysMani with a baseline; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: PhysMani 45.9%, 3DFA 37.8%, 3DDA 35.1%, Act3D 27.1%, ManiGaussian 22.5%, π0.5 8.3% mean success
status: Introduced inside a method paper; code and data repository listed; cited by MotionForge
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Mostly 3D policies; π0.5 is the only VLA baseline.

name: LIBERO-Plus
evaluates: Robustness of LIBERO-trained VLAs to seven controlled perturbation types: object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language instruction, lighting, background texture, sensor noise
improves: Near-ceiling LIBERO scores hide brittleness; earlier robustness tests used few scenarios and gave no fine-grained analysis within a perturbation dimension
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo); Franka Panda
scale: 10,030 perturbed test tasks; 7 dimensions with 21 sub-dimensions; 5 difficulty levels; 20K+ training trajectories released
policies: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT (three variants), π0, π0-FAST, NORA, WorldVLA, UniVLA, RIPT-VLA; success falls from about 95% to below 30%; camera and initial-state shifts hurt most, language changes least
status: Widely reused (LIBERO-MAX, LIBERO-Safety, IndustrialVLA-Bench, RoboTwin 2.0-Plus study); results table maintained in the GitHub README
note: ArXiv title is 'In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models'; the CVPR 2026 poster page lists it as 'A Progressive Robustness Benchmark for Visual-Language-Action Models'. The CVF open-access page returned 403.

name: LIBERO-PRO
evaluates: Whether LIBERO success reflects memorization, by perturbing object attributes, initial positions, task instructions and environments, alone and in combination
improves: The standard LIBERO train and test configuration lets overfitted models score near-perfectly while collapsing under small changes
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo)
scale: 4 perturbation dimensions applied to the LIBERO suites; task count not extracted
policies: OpenVLA, π0, π0.5; over 90% on standard LIBERO falls to 0.0% under the generalized setting; π0.5 retains 0.38 on position changes
status: Code released; reused by LIBERO-MAX (2,400 cases) and cited by most later LIBERO variants
note: No venue on the arXiv record.

name: LIBERO-X
evaluates: Robustness under coupled, multi-factor shifts graded in five levels: local spatial, extended spatial, scene topology, visual attributes, semantically equivalent instructions
improves: Existing benchmarks test isolated shifts, and LIBERO test sets closely mirror low-diversity training data
setup: MuJoCo; LIBERO-style environments; single arm with gripper
scale: 600 tasks in 100 scenes; 2,520 VR-teleoperated demonstrations; 5 perturbation levels; 4 multi-label task attributes
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, π0, X-VLA, GR00T-N1.5, π0.5; π0.5 falls from 65.2% (level 1) to 18.0% (level 5); three-step tasks near zero
status: Project page available; no leaderboard or code URL found

name: LIBERO-VPro
evaluates: Closed-loop visual robustness when the visual evidence itself is corrupted during execution: degradation, camera staleness, cross-view inconsistency, task-relevant scene variation
improves: Earlier suites perturb scene or task configuration while the observation stream stays temporally coherent and internally consistent
setup: LIBERO (40 tasks from four suites); real checks on Franka Research 3
scale: 40 tasks; 4 dimensions, 12 challenge categories, 96 settings, 3,296 task-condition cases; about 196,000 simulated episodes
real_check: π0.5 and LaWAM were run on a Franka Research 3 under four of the conditions (10 trials per condition, 200 rollouts); trends were reported as broadly consistent with simulation, without a correlation coefficient.
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0.5 and three world-action models (FastWAM, LingBot-VA, LaWAM); nominal 92-99% falls to 56-67% on average; view loss and stale cameras are most disruptive
status: Project page available; new preprint

name: LIBERO-Occ
evaluates: Robustness to scene-induced occlusion of the manipulated object, the receptacle, or both, at three severity levels
improves: VLA benchmarks implicitly assume task-relevant objects are fully visible in the input observation
setup: LIBERO (four suites); Franka arm
scale: 2,000 occluded task instances (500 per suite); 3 occlusion types x 3 severities
policies: OpenVLA-OFT 95.75% to 47.95%, π0.5 90.00% to 40.55%, UniVLA 88.25% to 57.10%; the proposed VIM reaches 65.05%
status: Code repository listed; benchmark-plus-method paper
note: The extraction named PyBullet as the engine, which conflicts with other LIBERO-derived papers (robosuite / MuJoCo); engine left unconfirmed.

name: LIBERO-MAX
evaluates: Task completion when the world changes after the policy has begun acting: target or receptacle relocation, camera shift, lighting switch, noise onset, distractors, obstacle insertion
improves: Existing benchmarks set external conditions at reset, so mid-episode change is untested
setup: LIBERO; cases drawn from LIBERO-Plus (5,600) and LIBERO-PRO (2,400)
scale: 8,000 Base/Dynamic pairs (16,000 rollouts per policy); 8 event types with 1,000 pairs each
policies: 14 policies including π0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, X-VLA, Xiaomi-Robotics-0, MolmoAct2, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.7, VLA-JEPA and five WAMs; every policy loses 11.0-25.7 points; WAMs are not consistently better or worse than VLAs
status: Project page available; new preprint

name: LIBERO-RECOVER
evaluates: Failure recovery in four difficulty levels: action retry, action adaptation, object-state recovery, environmental recovery
improves: Benchmarks evaluate completion from predefined initial states and do not assess failure recognition, state recovery or replanning
setup: LIBERO (robosuite / MuJoCo); Franka
scale: 130 subtasks across 4 suites; 2,178 recovery scenarios; 4 recovery levels; 10 trials per scenario
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, GR00T-N1.5, π0, π0-FAST, Wan2-Policy, Cosmos-Predict2-Policy; all lose more than half of their performance after failures; recovery success about 40% at level 1 and about 3% at level 4
status: Release announced, no URL found

name: LIBERO-CTRL
evaluates: Compound robustness: whether outcomes under simultaneous perturbations can be predicted from outcomes under each single perturbation on the same matched instance
improves: LIBERO-Plus tested selected pairwise combinations but did not link constituent and compound outcomes per evaluation instance
setup: LIBERO (four suites)
scale: 40 tasks; 6 axes (camera, lighting, robot pose, sensor, actuation, language); 3 severity levels; 400 matched configurations; 10,400 rollouts per checkpoint
policies: π0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, SmolVLA, VLA-JEPA, PredVLA, MINERVA; up to 29.0% of configurations change outcome between single-axis conjunction and the simultaneous condition while the aggregate barely moves
status: Code and per-rollout outcomes in a public repository; new preprint
note: Paper title is 'Beyond Single-Axis Testing: Paired Evaluation of Compound Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Policies'.

name: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus
evaluates: Robustness of bimanual policies, comparing world-action models with VLAs, under noise, lighting, camera, robot initial state, background, layout and language perturbations
improves: The LIBERO-Plus perturbation protocol existed only for single-arm LIBERO, and WAM-versus-VLA robustness had not been compared
setup: RoboTwin 2.0; Aloha-AgileX dual arm; paired with LIBERO-Plus for single-arm results
scale: 7 perturbation types; task count not extracted
policies: LingBot-VA 74.2%, Fast-WAM 72.7%, MOTUS 71.5%, π0.5 58.6%, X-VLA 53.1% overall; WAMs hold up under visual perturbations but struggle with camera and robot-state changes
status: Evaluation code page listed; introduced inside a study paper
note: Paper title is 'Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study'.

name: Eva-VLA
evaluates: Worst-case robustness to physically plausible variations found by black-box optimization: 3D object transformations, illumination changes, adversarial patches
improves: Adversarial-patch studies violate physical plausibility or need gradient access and do not cover the range of real physical variation
setup: LIBERO (four suites); real checks on an AgileX Piper
scale: 40 tasks; 3 variation families with 9 continuous parameters; 500 rollouts per suite
real_check: Three 'put A into B' tasks, one per variation type, were run on an AgileX Piper and failures were reported as consistent with simulation; no correlation statistic.
policies: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, π0.5; failure rates rise to 68-88% under 3D transformations; OpenVLA exceeds 90% failure on LIBERO-Long
status: No code or project URL found

name: VLATest
evaluates: Generation-based fuzz testing of VLAs over target and confounding objects, lighting, camera pose, unseen objects and instruction mutations
improves: VLA evaluation relied on small hand-made scene sets, with no automated testing framework
setup: ManiSkill2 with visual-matching rendering; tasks follow Open X-Embodiment-trained model setups; robot not specified in the extracted text
scale: 4 tasks; 18,604 generated scenes; 10 testing operators
policies: RT-1 (three checkpoints), RT-1-X, Octo-small, Octo-base, OpenVLA-7b; average success 12.4%, 6.0%, 1.2% and 0.5% on the four tasks; only 34% of passing cases survive camera mutations
status: Code and the 18,604 generated scenes released; LADEV evaluates the same seven models
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: LADEV
evaluates: Automated robustness testing in which scenes are generated from natural-language descriptions and instructions are paraphrased
improves: There was no platform for automatically testing and evaluating VLA models
setup: SAPIEN / ManiSkill2; extends SimplerEnv
scale: 4 tasks; 4,000+ generated scenes; multiple paraphrased instructions per scene
policies: RT-1 (three checkpoints), RT-1-X, Octo-small, Octo-base, OpenVLA-7b; success drops 10-30% on unseen objects and 5-15% under paraphrase; put-on and put-in tasks near zero
status: Project site available; code release was pending in the paper

name: PVEP (Manipulation Facing Threats)
evaluates: Physical visual threats to VLAs: blur, noise, brightness, typographic visual prompts, and adversarial patches from black-box to white-box
improves: No earlier work had evaluated open-source VLA models against physical security threats
setup: VIMA simulator and SimplerEnv
scale: 20 tasks (14 VIMA, 6 SimplerEnv); 4 threat categories
policies: LLaRA and OpenVLA; blur raises failure by about 47 points for both; white-box patches reach 94.5% (LLaRA) and 100% (OpenVLA) failure
status: Project page available

name: AttackVLA
evaluates: A common protocol for adversarial and backdoor attacks on VLAs, measuring effectiveness, transferability and targeted long-horizon misbehaviour
improves: Attacks were evaluated on different models and setups with no unified framework
setup: LIBERO (four suites); real tests on a 7-DoF Franka
scale: 40 tasks; 6 adversarial and 3 backdoor attacks
real_check: TMA, TabVLA and BackdoorVLA were run against π0-FAST on a Franka arm (attack success 42.5%, 20% and 50%); replication of attacks, no sim-real correlation.
policies: OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, π0-FAST; targeted backdoor success 75.35%, 51.63% and 48.23%; π0-FAST is the most robust to adversarial attacks
status: No code or project URL found

name: RoboStress
evaluates: Robustness to robot execution errors from mechanics: Stribeck friction, gear backlash, joint compliance, gravity-compensation error
improves: Robustness studies inject synthetic action noise and leave execution errors from the robot itself unexplored
setup: MuJoCo 3.7.0 with robosuite 1.4.1; LIBERO (four suites); real tests on AgileX Piper arms
scale: 40 tasks; 4 error types combined into 7 deployment scenarios
real_check: A self-compensating VLA was tested on two AgileX Piper arms with different wear on four tasks (76% vs 43% for the base policy on one arm); method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: π0 and π0.5 with domain-randomization and RobustVLA baselines; base π0.5 49.1% and π0 41.7% under stress; self-compensation raises them to 56.6% and 44.2%
status: Code release announced, no URL found
note: Paper title is 'Taming VLAs under Robot Execution Errors: Self-Compensation and Stress Testing'.

name: RoboTwin-Phys
evaluates: Sensitivity to physical-parameter variation: mass, centre of mass, friction, restitution, joint damping, table tilt and height, external force
improves: Benchmarks randomize appearance and layout but keep physical parameters at nominal values
setup: RoboTwin 2.0; bimanual
scale: 50 tasks; 13 physical dimensions; 5,000+ expert episodes annotated with physical parameters
policies: Fast-WAM 91.88% to 44.24%, Motus 88.66% to 39.60%, FACT 88.40% to 39.14%, Galaxea G0.5 93.70% to 37.82%, π0.5 82.74% to 31.60% (clean vs physical randomization)
status: Technical report; no code URL found
note: ArXiv comment describes it as a 'technical report for a benchmark'.

name: NEBULA
evaluates: Per-capability diagnosis (control, perception, language, dynamic adaptation, spatial reasoning, robustness) plus stress tests of inference frequency, latency, stability and adaptability
improves: A single end-task success metric gives no skill diagnosis and no measure of robustness to perturbation; data formats are fragmented
setup: SAPIEN / ManiSkill3; single-arm tasks; unified data from ManiSkill, LeRobot and BEHAVIOR-1K formats
scale: 6 capability families at 3 difficulty levels; 4 stress tests at 3 pressure levels; about 216,000 trajectories
policies: GR00T-N1.5, SpatialVLA, RDT-1B, MT-ACT, Diffusion Policy, ACT; perception and language are strong, spatial reasoning is weak, dynamic adaptation and robustness scores are near zero
status: Project page available; no leaderboard or code URL found
note: Task count was not clearly stated in the extracted text.

name: VLA-Arena
evaluates: Structured difficulty along task structure, language and vision, covering safety constraints, distractors, extrapolation to unseen objects and compositions, and long horizons
improves: Earlier benchmarks are static task collections that do not integrate robustness with extrapolation and overlook safety
setup: MuJoCo; LIBERO-style BDDL task definitions; Franka
scale: 170 tasks in 11 suites under 4 dimensions (Safety, Distractor, Extrapolation, Long Horizon); levels L0-L2; language W0-W4 and vision V0-V4; datasets with 10, 30 or 50 trajectories per task
real_check: Policies were run on a Franka Research 3 on tasks from all four dimensions; degradation with difficulty and failure modes matched simulation qualitatively, with no correlation coefficient.
policies: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0-FAST, UniVLA, SmolVLA; steep degradation from L0 to L2; high success is often reached by violating safety constraints
status: Open-source framework with leaderboard on the project site; reused by BeSafe-Bench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: RoboView-Bias
evaluates: Visual bias in grasping agents: how success varies with object colour, camera orientation and pose, distance, shape and initial position
improves: Benchmarks emphasize generalization and perturbation robustness, with little systematic quantification of visual bias
setup: RoboVerse with MuJoCo backend; single arm; grasping only
scale: 2,127 task instances; factors include 141 colours, 9 camera orientations, 21 camera poses, 9 distance scales
policies: VLM-driven agents MOKA and SimpleAgent (GPT-4o, Qwen-VL-Max) and π0; π0 46.53% average success with 53.05% coefficient of variation across factors
status: No code or project URL found
note: Only one VLA (π0) is evaluated.

name: GemBench
evaluates: Generalization of vision-language manipulation policies in four levels: new placements, new rigid objects, new articulated objects, unseen long-horizon tasks
improves: RLBench-style evaluation tests seen tasks; VIMA-Bench has simple skills and Colosseum targets environment perturbations rather than new tasks
setup: RLBench (CoppeliaSim); real tests on a UR5
scale: 16 training tasks (31 variations, 3,100 demonstrations); 44 test tasks (92 variations) in 4 levels; 7 action primitives
real_check: 3D-LOTUS and 3D-LOTUS++ were trained on 20 demos per variation for 7 real variations on a UR5 and tested on 7 seen and 7 unseen variations; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: Hiveformer, PolarNet, RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, 3D-LOTUS, 3D-LOTUS++ (no VLA in the original paper); level 1 up to 94.3%, level 4 at most 0.3% except 3D-LOTUS++ at 17.4%
status: Code and dataset public; project page maintained by the authors; 3D-LOTUS++ from this paper is a baseline in AGNOSTOS and ArtiBench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. The extraction called RLBench 'PyBullet-based', which conflicts with other RLBench papers (CoppeliaSim).

name: AGNOSTOS
evaluates: Zero-shot cross-task generalization to unseen tasks in two levels: partial semantic overlap with training tasks, and entirely novel scenarios
improves: Existing benchmarks assess within-task generalization and leave zero-shot cross-task generalization unexplored
setup: RLBench; real tests on an xArm7 with DH-Robotics gripper
scale: 18 seen RLBench tasks (3,600 demonstrations); 23 unseen tasks (13 level-1, 10 level-2)
real_check: The proposed X-ICM was tested zero-shot on five real tasks on an xArm7 (20 executions per task) using demos from other tasks; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: PerAct, RVT, RVT-2, Sigma-Agent, Instant Policy, R3M, D4R, OpenVLA, RDT, π0, LLARVA, SAM2Act, 3D-LOTUS++, VoxPoser, X-ICM; π0 17.5% on unseen tasks, X-ICM (72B) 30.1%
status: Project page and code available; no venue on the arXiv record
note: The extracted margins over π0 were not mutually consistent, so only the absolute numbers are given.

name: HiMan-Bench (RoboHiMan)
evaluates: Compositional generalization in long-horizon manipulation under perturbation, separating planning failure from execution failure via vanilla, decoupled and coupled evaluation modes
improves: Existing benchmarks cannot tell whether failures come from planning, execution or sensitivity to environmental perturbation
setup: CoppeliaSim / PyRep; extends DeCoBench tasks with Colosseum perturbation factors; Franka Panda
scale: 258 tasks (114 atomic and 144 compositional, including perturbed versions); 12 perturbation factors; 4 progressive training-data levels
real_check: π0.5 was run on a Mobile ALOHA arm on 4 atomic and 4 compositional tasks with distractor, position and human-intervention perturbations (vanilla 17.5% to 10%, with rule-based planner 47.5% to 27.5%); qualitative replication only.
policies: RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, π0, π0.5; near-zero on compositional tasks without a planner; with a rule-based planner RVT-2 reaches 39.5%; VLM planners lag rule-based ones
status: Project page available; listed as under review

name: DeCoBench
evaluates: Zero-shot composition of learned atomic skills into unseen long-horizon 3D manipulation sequences
improves: Multi-task imitation policies trained on atomic tasks fail on longer compositions, and no benchmark isolated this
setup: RLBench; Franka Emika Panda
scale: 10 atomic tasks (50 demonstrations each); 12 compositional long-horizon tasks
real_check: DeCo-augmented policies were trained on 6 real atomic tasks and tested on 9 novel long-horizon tasks (53.33% vs 0% without DeCo); method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: RVT-2, 3D Diffuser Actor, ARP (3D policies, no VLA); baselines are near 0% on compositional tasks; with DeCo 66.67%, 21.53% and 58.06%
status: Project page available; extended by HiMan-Bench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment ('RAL 2026'). Introduced inside the DeCo method paper.

name: ClevrSkills
evaluates: Compositional generalization: whether models trained on simple motor skills can compose them for intermediate and complex tasks, including low-level execution
improves: VIMA-style benchmarks test high-level planning and not closed-loop plan-and-execute with low-level control
setup: ManiSkill2; UFACTORY xArm 6 with vacuum gripper (Franka Panda also available)
scale: 33 tasks in 3 levels (12 simple, 15 intermediate, 6 complex); about 330K trajectories
policies: JAT, RoboFlamingo, Octo, StreamRoboLM; level-0 success 24-63%; level 1 and level 2 stay at or below about 6% even after fine-tuning
status: Code and dataset released by Qualcomm AI Research
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: INT-ACT
evaluates: Generalization boundaries of VLAs along object diversity, language complexity and vision-language reasoning, separating correct intention from successful execution
improves: SimplerEnv has few tasks, and imitation-learning benchmarks lack language variation
setup: ManiSkill2 / SimplerEnv (expanded from 4 to 50 BridgeV2 tasks); WidowX
scale: 50 tasks; 3 categories with 10 sub-categories
policies: π0 (fine-tuned, from scratch, with rephrasing), SpatialVLA, Magma, Octo; intention is correct in 80-100% of cases while task success drops sharply on out-of-distribution variants
status: Project page and code available; arXiv comment says under review

name: LIBERO-OOD
evaluates: Out-of-distribution recombination of skills seen in training: tasks that require stitching sub-trajectories never shown together
improves: There was no benchmark of tasks that VLAs could plausibly complete but currently cannot; standard LIBERO is near ceiling
setup: LIBERO; derived from the goal, object and spatial suites
scale: 20 extrapolated tasks (10 goal-ood, 10 spatial-ood)
policies: π0 9%, π0-FAST 15%, OpenVLA-OFT 1%, UniVLA 21%; text-latent interpolation raises π0 to 83%
status: Code released; introduced inside a study paper
note: Paper title is 'VLAs are Confined yet Capable of Generalizing to Novel Instructions'.

name: RoboCAS
evaluates: Picking, selecting and searching in scattered, orderly and stacked object arrangements that require obstacle clearance and reasoning about chain reactions
improves: Embodied models are rarely tested on grasping in complex object arrangements
setup: SAPIEN (PhysX); Franka Emika Panda on a mobile base
scale: 3 tasks; 3 arrangement types; 7,300 trajectory episodes
policies: RT-1 34.2%, 23.3% and 10.2% (scattered, orderly, stacked); RoboFlamingo 15.6%, 13.3% and 0%
status: Code and dataset released; little later use seen

name: ArtiBench
evaluates: Articulated-object manipulation in five levels: random placement, novel parts, novel instances, novel categories, long-horizon composition
improves: Datasets rarely evaluate cross-part, cross-instance or cross-category generalization in sequential articulated interactions
setup: CoppeliaSim / PyRep; assets from PartNet-Mobility, RLBench and YCB
scale: 132 articulated scenes with 449 variations; 5 levels; 50 demonstrations per task
real_check: The proposed ArtiBrain was run on a Franka Research 3 on door, drawer and composed tasks; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: 3D-LOTUS, 3D-LOTUS++ (35.8% average), AffordDP, ArtiBrain (60.0% on novel parts); only ArtiBrain completes the long-horizon level
status: Code and dataset release announced on acceptance
note: No VLA baseline.

name: Behavior-Skill
evaluates: Skill-level evaluation inside long-horizon household tasks, locating which constituent skills cause task failure
improves: BEHAVIOR-style data is annotated only at task level, so constituent skills cannot be evaluated separately
setup: OmniGibson; BEHAVIOR-1K; 23-DoF bimanual mobile manipulator
scale: 50 household tasks; 235,492 skill instances in 34 skill categories; 10,000 demonstrations; 500 evaluation episodes
policies: π0.5 42.4% and GR00T N1.7 36.9% task-level score, 48.4% and 42.5% with skill-level conditioning; contact-rich skills (open lid, close door, pour) are persistent bottlenecks
status: Code released; new preprint

name: RoboCerebra
evaluates: Deliberative long-horizon manipulation: planning, reflection and memory over episodes of thousands of steps, with disturbances and observation mismatches
improves: Earlier long-horizon benchmarks involve 2-5 sub-tasks and fewer than 500 action steps
setup: LIBERO; household scenes; hierarchical VLM planner plus VLA controller protocol
scale: 1,000 human-annotated trajectories over 100 task variants; 2,972 steps on average; 6 sub-task types (ideal, memory exploration, memory execution, random disturbance, observation mismatching, mix)
policies: OpenVLA as controller with GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL or LLaVA-Next-Video as planner; best VLM planner 16.04% average success, ground-truth plan 25.16%
status: Code, dataset and benchmark files released; no leaderboard
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: MemoryBench (SAM2Act)
evaluates: Spatial memory and action recall in tasks built to violate the Markov assumption: identical observations require different actions depending on history
improves: RLBench-style tasks do not test memory-dependent behaviour
setup: RLBench (CoppeliaSim / PyRep); Franka Emika Panda
scale: 3 tasks (reopen_drawer, put_block_back, rearrange_block); 100 training and 25 test demonstrations per task
real_check: One real memory task ('push the same button') on a Franka Panda: SAM2Act+ 70% in-distribution vs RVT-2 40%; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: RVT-2 54.0%, SAM2Act 55.0%, SAM2Act+ 94.3% (3D keyframe policies, no VLA in the original paper)
status: SAM2Act+ is a baseline in later memory benchmarks (RoboMME, HIDE); RMBench criticizes MemoryBench's reproducibility and task design
note: Introduced inside the SAM2Act method paper; no venue on the arXiv record.

name: MIKASA-Robo
evaluates: Memory-dependent tabletop skills in four categories: object memory, spatial memory, sequential memory, memory capacity
improves: Memory methods were tested on bespoke environments, which fragmented comparison
setup: ManiSkill3; tabletop arm; Gymnasium API
scale: 32 tasks in 12 groups; 1,000 expert trajectories per task for offline learning
real_check: Three tasks were run on an SO-101 arm; results mirrored the simulation ordering, failing once long occlusion is introduced; no correlation statistic.
policies: RL baselines (PPO-MLP, PPO-LSTM, SAC, TD-MPC2, Decision Transformer, RATE, Diffusion Policy) and VLAs Octo, OpenVLA, π0, SpatialVLA; success falls to near zero as memory demands grow
status: Pip-installable; code and datasets public; extended by MIKASA-Robo-VLA
note: Venue from the project page. Built for RL first; VLA results were added in later versions.

name: MIKASA-Robo-VLA
evaluates: What a language-conditioned policy must remember and for how long, over ten memory types including temporal, negative, procedural, prospective and tracking
improves: CALVIN and LIBERO stress skill composition without controlling memory content or duration, and memory suites cover few memory types
setup: ManiSkill3; extends MIKASA-Robo; arm with gripper at 10 Hz
scale: 90 language-conditioned tasks in 26 families; 10 memory types; 22,500 oracle episodes (6.3M frames)
policies: π0.5 fine-tuned on a 14-task subset: 0.211 mean success, 0.017 on long-split tasks; OpenVLA and muVLA numbers are cited from other work
status: Code and RLDS / LeRobot datasets released; new preprint

name: RoboMME
evaluates: Four kinds of memory in manipulation: temporal (counting, ordering), spatial (tracking under occlusion), object (referential identity), procedural (reproducing motions)
improves: Existing benchmarks neither capture realistic memory demands nor provide a standard testbed for memory-augmented policies
setup: ManiSkill; Franka Panda; front and wrist cameras
scale: 16 tasks in 4 suites (Counting, Permanence, Reference, Imitation); 1,600 demonstrations (770K timesteps)
real_check: Four real tasks mirroring the simulated ones were run with two memory variants (25/40 and 19/40 successes); patterns were reported as similar to simulation, without a correlation coefficient.
policies: 14 memory variants built on π0.5, plus π0.5, SAM2Act+ and MemER; best learned variant 44.51%, oracle symbolic memory 84.08%; no single memory design wins on all tasks
status: Project page available; extended by RoboMME-Interference and RoboIRGBench; memory module reused in MEMOBench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: RoboMME-Interference
evaluates: Long-context robot memory when irrelevant earlier sessions sit between the relevant demonstration and the query
improves: Robot-memory benchmarks measure single episodes or short contexts, not cross-session interference
setup: Extends RoboMME (ManiSkill)
scale: 9 task families; 0, 1, 3 or 7 distractor sessions
policies: 12 memory systems built on π0.5; one variant falls from a 27.1-point gain to 19.3% with 7 distractors; a retrieval-based variant stays at 44.7-44.9%
status: Project site listed; new preprint

name: RMBench
evaluates: Memory-dependent bimanual manipulation graded by how many past observations must be retained: one (M(1)) or several (M(n))
improves: MemoryBench is hard to reproduce, MIKASA targets RL, and LIBERO-Long tasks need no memory because all information stays visible
setup: SAPIEN; RoboTwin 2.0 platform (also implemented on Isaac Lab-Arena); dual arm
scale: 9 tasks (5 M(1), 4 M(n)); 50 demonstrations per task
real_check: Three tasks were run on an X-One dual-arm platform with 100 demonstrations (Mem-0 22.5%, π0.5 5.83%, ACT 0%); method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: Diffusion Policy, ACT, π0.5, X-VLA, Mem-0; best baseline X-VLA 11.8% on M(1) and 7.3% on M(n); Mem-0 42.0% overall
status: Hosted under the RoboTwin platform organization; code public

name: RoboMemArena
evaluates: Memory in long, partially observable tasks: transferring, occlusion, counting and sequence, with keyframe-level annotations of what must be remembered
improves: Earlier memory benchmarks lack annotations for memory formation, have limited task coverage and stay in simulation
setup: Simulation plus matching real tasks; dual-arm AgileX Cobot Mobile ALOHA for the real set
scale: 26 simulated tasks and 5 real tasks; 1,076 steps per task on average; 2,600 demonstrations; 68.9% of subtasks memory-dependent
real_check: Five real tasks with 10 rollouts each: π0.5 20%, MemER 40%, PrediMem 52%; these extend the benchmark to hardware, and no sim-real correlation is reported.
policies: π0.5 21.5%, HiF-VLA 16.9%, MemoryVLA 15.0%, MemER 27.3%, PrediMem 38.5% task success; frozen Qwen3-VL and GPT-5.4 planners 6.0% and 8.7%
status: Project page with leaderboard, code, dataset and weights listed
note: The simulator was not named explicitly in the extracted text.

name: MEMOBench
evaluates: Process-level memory operations (storage, update, compression) measured at executable checkpoints, separately from task success
improves: Final task success conflates forgetting with manipulation failure, which makes memory errors hard to diagnose
setup: LIBERO / robosuite (MuJoCo) with BDDL task definitions
scale: 30 history-dependent tasks; 1,500 demonstrations; 84 checkpoint templates giving 4,200 instances
policies: π0 11.2%, π0.5 30.4%, OpenVLA-OFT 10.0%, MemoryVLA 17.2%, HiF-VLA 21.0%, π0.5 with RoboMME memory module 31.9% success; storage rates are high while update and compression rates stay low
status: Code and annotations released

name: HIDE
evaluates: Skill-level memory at decision points where similar observations need different actions: repetition counting, historical-state recall, execution-progress tracking
improves: Benchmarks stress completion and generalization and do not isolate the historical information a decision needs
setup: RLBench (CoppeliaSim / PyRep); Franka Emika Panda; 4 RGB-D cameras
scale: 15 tasks (5 per category); 100 demonstrations and 25 test episodes per task
real_check: Four real tasks on a Franka Panda with 25 trials each: SEEK 89%, SAM2Act+ 47%, π0.5 13%; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
status: Project page available; benchmark-plus-method paper
note: Paper title is 'Benchmarking and Enhancing Skill-Level Memory for Partially Observable Robotic Manipulation'.

name: LIBERO-Mem
evaluates: Object-level memory under partial observability: tracking interaction history across visually identical objects, object permanence and order
improves: RLBench, LIBERO and RoboCasa focus on short-horizon or atomic tasks and overlook non-Markovian settings
setup: LIBERO; extends LIBERO-Goal
scale: 10 tasks over four memory dimensions; 120 trajectories per task; 200-700 frames per task
policies: π0 and SlotVLA baselines average about 5.0% subgoal completion; the proposed Embodied-SlotSSM reaches 14.8%
status: Dataset on Hugging Face; code repositories listed
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Introduced inside a method paper ('Rethinking Progression of Memory State in Robotic Manipulation').

name: RuleSafe
evaluates: Long-horizon, non-Markovian articulated manipulation: opening safes whose locks follow multi-step rules with dependencies between joints
improves: Simulation benchmarks are mostly short-horizon and lack multi-joint dependencies
setup: SAPIEN; built on HumanoidGen; Unitree H1-2 with Inspire hands
scale: 20 lock rules; 10 safe instances; 1,000 trajectories (638 frames on average)
policies: DP3 45.0%, RDT 35.0%, CogACT 20.0%, π0 80.0% on the simplest rule; multi-task π0 gains 31.3 points with the proposed VQ-Memory
status: Project page available; introduced inside a method paper

name: COIN
evaluates: Interactive reasoning under partial observability: acting to gather information, updating beliefs and adapting the plan
improves: Existing benchmarks do not systematically evaluate reasoning that depends on continued interaction with the environment
setup: ManiSkill3; Franka Emika Panda
scale: 90 tasks (50 interactive, 20 primitive, 20 composition); 1,000+ demonstrations for primitives
policies: Hierarchical GPT-4o or Gemini 2.0 Flash planners with GR00T N1, π0 or CogACT: 1.5-2.2% on COIN-50; ReKep 3.26%; end-to-end VLAs 16-19% on primitives; human teleoperation 40%
status: No code or project URL found

name: RoboSPA
evaluates: Fine-grained spatial reasoning and long-horizon procedural planning at five difficulty levels of rising spatial ambiguity and procedural complexity
improves: Benchmarks measure completion under fixed settings and say little about reasoning as spatial and procedural complexity grows
setup: RoboTwin 2.0 framework (SAPIEN with CuRobo); five embodiments (Aloha-AgileX, ARX-X5, Piper, Franka, UR5)
scale: 56 base tasks in 10 categories x 5 levels = 280 variants; 527K trajectories
policies: Four VLA models (names not extracted) in single-task settings on Aloha-AgileX; all stay below 25% overall success at the highest level
status: Code and dataset on GitHub and Hugging Face
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. The arXiv HTML returned 404; details come from the abstract and the GitHub README.

name: ActiveArena
evaluates: Active perception: moving head and torso or interacting with objects to obtain missing evidence, and retaining it across views
improves: Benchmarks do not require seeking missing evidence or selectively keeping information as observations accumulate
setup: Own simulator extending RoboTwin 2.0 (PhysX); Astribot S1 dual-arm humanoid with controllable head and torso
scale: 35 tasks in 2 families and 5 categories; 100 trajectories per task; 50 seeds per task for in- and out-of-distribution evaluation
real_check: Eight tasks on a physical Astribot with 20 trials per policy per task; ordering was consistent with simulation (best variant 55.6%, MemER 34.4%, π0.5 23.8%), without a correlation coefficient.
policies: FAST-WAM, π0.5, SaPaVe, HiF-VLA, MemER, MemoryVLA and 13 in-house variants; best 62.97% in-distribution and 47.60% out-of-distribution; MemER 35.31% and 23.43%
status: Project page with code; results table in the paper

name: BAVO-Bench
evaluates: Recovering from unexpected, externally caused occlusion by moving an active camera arm during bimanual manipulation
improves: Active-vision work studied viewpoint needs set by task geometry, not recovery from unexpected visibility loss
setup: AV-ALOHA simulation platform; manipulation arm plus camera arm
scale: 5 multi-stage tasks; 100 VR demonstrations per task; 3 visibility conditions (clean, stage occlusion, random-time occlusion)
real_check: A representative rollout of the proposed A-FAR on a Piper arm with a camera arm; demonstration only, no quantitative sim-real comparison.
policies: ACT, ManiFlow, π0.5, A-FAR; under random-time occlusion A-FAR 18.7% vs ManiFlow 15.0%; π0.5 falls from 42% to 4.0%
status: Project page available

name: VLABench
evaluates: Language-conditioned manipulation that needs world knowledge, implicit-intent instructions, spatial and physical understanding and multi-step reasoning
improves: RLBench, CALVIN and LIBERO use templated instructions and do not test knowledge transfer or long-horizon reasoning in VLAs
setup: MuJoCo with dm_control; Franka Emika Panda by default
scale: 100 task categories (60 primitive, 40 composite); 2,164 objects in 163 categories; 6 evaluation dimensions
policies: OpenVLA 11.74% seen and 7.93% unseen, Octo 1.34% and 0.77%, RDT-1B 15.37% and 9.08%; VoxPoser and CoPA workflows and seven VLMs also tested
status: Used as an evaluation suite by later VLA papers and as the base of HazardArena; standard evaluation tracks in the repository
note: Venue from the GitHub README.

name: LIBERO-Para
evaluates: Paraphrase robustness with action expressions and object references varied independently, scored by a difficulty-weighted index (PRIDE)
improves: Earlier tests treat paraphrasing as unstructured sentence-level variation or mix it with changes of task semantics
setup: LIBERO-Goal (with a cross-check on CALVIN)
scale: 4,092 paraphrases of 10 instructions; 43 paraphrase-type combinations on 2 axes
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, π0.5, Xiaomi-Robotics-0, X-VLA, VLA-Adapter (7 configurations); success drops 22.8-51.9 points; object-level lexical variation hurts most; 79.5-95.5% of failures are planning-level
status: Code and benchmark public; reused by IndustrialVLA-Bench
note: Venue from the arXiv comment (main conference, oral).

name: LangGap
evaluates: Whether policies read the instruction: several semantically different tasks share one tabletop layout
improves: LIBERO assigns one task per layout, so tasks can be solved by visual memorization without language
setup: LIBERO (robosuite)
scale: 99 tasks (40 original, 59 added) over 4 perturbation dimensions: object category, target location, spatial description, drawer action
policies: π0.5, π0, π0-FAST, SmolVLA; π0.5 falls from 93.8% to 21.4% on the added tasks and to 0% on changed target location
status: Code repository listed

name: LIBERO-CF
evaluates: Counterfactual instruction following: visually plausible but linguistically different instructions in familiar LIBERO layouts
improves: No systematic benchmark separated language following from scene-specific visual shortcuts
setup: LIBERO; real tests on Franka Research 3 with Robotiq 2F-85
scale: 50 tasks in 4 suites (CF-Spatial 15, CF-Object 10, CF-Long 10, CF-OOD 15)
real_check: π0.5 with and without the proposed guidance was tested on a Franka Research 3 over five dimensions, 10 trials per instruction; method test, no sim-real correlation.
policies: OpenVLA-OFT 0.4%, π0 9.6%, π0.5 13.2%, X-VLA 13.8% success on counterfactual tasks, against 65-97% in-domain
status: Project page available; no venue on the arXiv record
note: Paper title is 'When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs'.

name: SimplerEnv-Instruct
evaluates: Zero-shot instruction following and situated reasoning with closed-loop control, in task-aggregation and situated-reasoning splits
improves: Manipulation benchmarks focus on atomic commands and low-level control and neglect contextual reasoning
setup: SimplerEnv; Google Robot and WidowX
scale: 80 tasks (50 task aggregation, 30 situated reasoning); 1.1K trials
real_check: The InstructVLA paper also reports zero-shot WidowX-250 and few-shot Franka Research 3 experiments for the method; these do not validate the benchmark.
policies: InstructVLA 46.2%, OpenVLA with fine-tuning and GPT 35.6%, Magma 23.8%, SpatialVLA 16.5%, π0 12.0%
status: Introduced inside the InstructVLA paper; project page available
note: No venue on the arXiv record (comment field: '48 pages').

name: InstructMove
evaluates: Instruction following where language is required to choose among visually and physically plausible distractors; counterfactual tests with absent targets or empty instructions
improves: Benchmarks rarely contain episodes in which the instruction is indispensable for selecting the target
setup: Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim; dual-arm PiperX and single-arm Franka
scale: 4 task families (category, attribute, spatial, compositional pick-place); 1,757 objects in 103 categories; 100 training and 100 held-out episodes per task
real_check: π0.5 was tested on a dual-arm PiperX with 5 real objects; adding 2,000 simulated demos to 200 real ones raised reach from 26/50 to 34/50; sim-to-real co-training study, no correlation.
policies: π0.5, GR00T N1.7, π0, Motus; π0.5 0.82 reach and 0.57 lift on category picking; with an absent target it still reaches some object 99% of the time
status: No code or project URL found

name: ConflictVLA-Bench
evaluates: Whether a VLA stops acting when the task premise is invalid: instruction-internal, object-grounding, spatial-relation and physical-feasibility conflicts
improves: Evaluation looks at terminal outcomes only; task failure does not show that the policy disengaged from an invalid goal
setup: LIBERO with controlled conflict injection
scale: 2,826 conflict tasks; 4 conflict types; 4 structural levels; 14,530 rollouts per model
policies: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0-FAST, π0.5, GR00T N1.7, VLA-JEPA, UniVLA; policies keep approaching the original target (approach ratios 0.586-0.741); premise-checking prompts do not help consistently
status: Code repository listed

name: RoboIRGBench
evaluates: Implicit referential grounding: identifying task-relevant entities named only through pronouns, spatial references, context or reasoning
improves: RLBench, CALVIN, LIBERO and RoboCasa instructions name targets explicitly
setup: Built on the RoboMME simulator (ManiSkill); real tests on Franka Research 3
scale: 40 variants of 11 tasks; 4 grounding categories; 3 difficulty levels
real_check: π0.5 and one memory variant were run on two tasks with 10 trials per condition on a Franka Research 3: 70-85% with explicit references, 5-10% with reasoning-mediated ones; small replication, no correlation.
policies: π0.5, FrameSamp-Modul, TTT-Expert, GroundSG-QwenVL, MemER; one variant falls from 45.82% (explicit) to 16.85% (reasoning-mediated)
status: Project page available

name: RoboSemanticBench
evaluates: Whether instruction semantics reach the action: the robot answers multiple-choice maths and knowledge questions by picking the correct block
improves: Templated commands cannot show whether the semantic competence of the pretrained backbone survives robot fine-tuning
setup: Tabletop simulation with Aloha-AgileX dual arm; simulator not named in the extracted text
scale: 3 question domains (500, 7,473 and 10,000 questions), each in 4-choice and 10-choice form (6 suites)
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, GO1, DexVLA, TinyVLA, PD-VLA, π0, π0.5, GR00T N1.7, QwenGR00T; grasp success 85-99% while task success sits near chance; best is π0.5 at 21.8%
status: Code repository listed

name: BeTTER
evaluates: Embodied reasoning under causal interventions: spatial layout shifts, primitive recomposition, adversarial distractor objects, temporal extrapolation
improves: Evaluation rewards behavioural competence without checking the underlying reasoning, and static assets limit systematic variation of task semantics
setup: Simulation (engine not named in the extracted text); real checks on an SO-101
scale: 10 base tasks expanded to 60 variations; 4 perturbation types
real_check: Short- and long-horizon tasks with target-absence and phase-conflict interventions were run on an SO-101; simulation findings were reported to persist, without a correlation statistic.
policies: π0.5, GR00T-N1.6, Being-H0.5; GR00T-N1.6 follows 100% of spatial but 5% of semantic instructions; 52.5% drop on unseen subgoal compositions
status: Project page available
note: Paper title is 'Unmasking the Illusion of Embodied Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models'.

name: LIBERO-VIFO
evaluates: Following authorized visual cues placed in the scene (text, symbols, ghost trajectories, gestures, signage, codes) while ignoring unauthorized ones
improves: Earlier cue-following tests covered few cue forms, scored only final success and treated every cue as authorized
setup: LIBERO (MuJoCo); real check on an AgileX PiPER
scale: 40 tasks; 8 cue families; 1,347 cue instances; 5,388 companion VQA questions
real_check: π0.5 was run on a cup-stacking task on an AgileX PiPER with authorized and conflicting cues; single-task replication, no correlation.
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, π0.5, MolmoAct2, Action-Sketcher, InstructVLA, InternVLA-A1.5, Xiaomi-Robotics-0; full-chain accuracy at most 17.6%; unauthorized cues induce actions in 32.2-60.1% of cases without language
status: No code or project URL found

name: KinDER
evaluates: Physical reasoning isolated from perception and language: spatial relations, nonprehensile multi-object manipulation, tool use, combinatorial geometric constraints, dynamic constraints
improves: Physical-reasoning ability is entangled with perception and language in existing benchmarks, and there is no agreed state of the art
setup: Four backends (pure Python 2D, Pymunk, PyBullet, MuJoCo); 3D robot is a TidyBot++ with Kinova Gen3 arm
scale: 25 procedurally generated environments (10 in 2D, 15 in 3D); demonstrations for 10 environments
real_check: A real-to-sim-to-real demonstration on a TidyBot++ planned in the simulator and executed on hardware; no policy benchmark on real robots and no correlation.
policies: 13 baselines: bilevel planning 0.57, LLM and VLM in-context 0.43, fine-tuned π0.5 0.32, Diffusion Policy 0.24, PPO 0.13, SAC 0.02 average success
status: Open-source site with code
note: Venue from the arXiv comment. Targets planning and learning methods broadly; π0.5 is the only VLA.

name: IMBench
evaluates: Intuitive physical manipulation in three stages (constraint understanding, action proposal, closed-loop execution): geometry, dynamics, causal chains, tool use, hidden state, replanning, stability
improves: Benchmarks test physical reasoning separately from execution, or measure policies without requiring reasoning
setup: Robosuite (MuJoCo); single-arm and bimanual Franka with parallel-jaw and suction grippers
scale: 35 tasks in 7 categories; about 14K trajectories
policies: Diffusion Policy 0.24, π0.5 0.15 and GR00T N1.5 0.02 mean success after fine-tuning (zero-shot at most 0.02); a GPT-based agent reaches 11.3% with vision
status: Project site available; full data and code release pending
note: Venue from the arXiv comment (workshop paper).

name: SafeVLA-Bench
evaluates: The gap between success and safe success: excessive contact, disturbing bystander objects, destabilizing held objects and self-contact, checked post hoc with temporal-logic specifications
improves: VLA benchmarks record binary completion and miss safety-relevant behaviour along the trajectory
setup: MuJoCo; wraps LIBERO and RoboCasa-365; Franka and Panda-with-Omron setups
scale: 58 tasks (40 LIBERO, 18 RoboCasa-365 families); 8 constraint families; about 18,000 episodes; metrics include success-but-unsafe rate and violation severity index
real_check: A pilot on an SO-101 arm with video-labelled checks of two constraint families found 4 unsafe successes among 26 successful rollouts; pilot only, no correlation.
policies: 18 policies on LIBERO and 9 on RoboCasa-365, including OpenVLA, π0, π0.5, GR00T N1.6/N1.7, X-VLA, SmolVLA, Cosmos-Policy; policies above 90% success still have 18-28% unsafe episodes; 38-56% of RoboCasa-365 successes violate a constraint
status: Project site available; code and data release announced

name: LIBERO-Safety
evaluates: Physical and semantic safety: affordance-aware grasping, human-robot interaction, tabletop avoidance, free-space hand and object avoidance, semantic safety reasoning
improves: Safety methods are tested under inconsistent protocols in static scenes with simple tabletop obstacles
setup: Extends LIBERO-Plus; Panda arm; collision-free demonstrations from a CuRobo keypose pipeline
scale: 75 tasks (5 suites x 5 tasks x 3 levels); 19,664 collision-free demonstrations
policies: OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0.5, UniVLA, VLA-JEPA, GR00T N1.5 and N1.6, plus RoboBrain2.0 and RynnBrain-CoP for refusal; π0.5 is best at 35-88% across suites
status: Project page available
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: SafeLIBERO
evaluates: Collision avoidance while completing LIBERO tasks, with obstacles placed near the target or across the motion path
improves: Objects rarely collide with the arm in the original LIBERO, so it contains no safety-critical scenarios
setup: Robosuite; LIBERO; Franka Emika Panda
scale: 16 tasks; 32 scenarios (2 obstacle levels per task); 1,600 episodes
real_check: Two tasks at two safety levels were run on a Franka Panda with π0.5-DROID and the proposed safety layer; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: π0.5 18.7% collision avoidance and 50.9% success; OpenVLA-OFT 15.1% and 22.8%; AEGIS 77.9% and 68.1%
status: Introduced inside the VLSA / AEGIS method paper; code and project page public
note: Venue from the arXiv comment.

name: Safety-CHORES
evaluates: Safety constraints in mobile manipulation: corners, blind spots, fragile collections, critical points and dangerous equipment
improves: Safe-RL benchmarks use simplified dynamics and VLA benchmarks measure success without built-in safety constraints
setup: AI2-THOR with ProcTHOR scenes and Objaverse assets; mobile robot with arm
scale: 3 task types (Safety-ObjNav, Safety-PickUp, Safety-Fetch); 150K procedurally generated scenes; 5 safety-critical component types
real_check: The aligned policy was deployed for Safety-PickUp on a platform with dual Realman RM75-6F arms; method transfer, no sim-real correlation.
policies: SPOC variants, EmbCLIP, Embodied-Codebook, FLaRe, PoliFormer and the proposed ISA; ISA cuts safety cost by 83.58% while keeping task performance
status: Introduced inside the SafeVLA method paper; project page with data and models
note: Venue from the arXiv comment (spotlight). Navigation-heavy mobile manipulation; baselines are SPOC-style policies, not tabletop VLAs.

name: HazardArena
evaluates: Semantic safety: whether a policy withholds an action that is motorically identical to a safe one but unsafe in its visual-linguistic context
improves: Evaluation measures completion and not whether the action was permissible in context
setup: MuJoCo; built on the VLABench task framework; Franka Panda
scale: 51 risk scenarios with safe and unsafe twins (10-task main suite); 7 hazard categories; 1,000 safe demonstrations
real_check: Five task families were run on a Franka Panda with 100 trials per condition using mitigated props: safe-only fine-tuning gave 46.0% safe and 39.6% unsafe success; refusal-augmented training cut unsafe success to 0.4%.
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, VLA-Adapter, NORA, π0; safe-only fine-tuning raises unsafe-twin execution together with safe success (π0: 0.47 safe, 0.44 unsafe)
status: No code or project URL found; listed as submitted

name: ForesightSafety-VLA
evaluates: Process-level safety across physical interaction (force, thermal, spatial boundary, collaboration, sequencing), instruction-side and perception-side hazards
improves: Safety is absent from VLA benchmarks, reduced to sparse collision checks, or mixed with generic task failure
setup: RoboTwin assets and task primitives; five embodiments
scale: 66 safety-augmented scenarios; 13 categories in three families; structure levels L0-L2, language W0-W4, vision V0-V4
policies: OpenVLA-OFT, RDT, Diffusion Policy, ACT with full metrics (safe success 0.42, 0.30, 0.24, 0.20); π0.5, π0, DexVLA and others in partial runs; no baseline is fully safe
status: No code or project URL found

name: SafeManip
evaluates: Temporal safety properties monitored on low-level rollouts: collision and contact, grasp and release stability, cross-contamination, action onset, mechanism, containment, enclosure
improves: Benchmarks cover either physical consequences or the semantic structure of safe behaviour, not temporal specifications on executed motion
setup: RoboCasa365 and LIBERO
scale: 90 tasks (50 RoboCasa365, 40 LIBERO); 8 property categories; 50 rollouts per task
policies: π0, π0.5, GR00T N1.5 and N1.6, RLDX-1, Cosmos Policy, OpenVLA; on RoboCasa365 more capable policies violate more (r = +0.66), on LIBERO the reverse (r = -0.99)
status: Code repository listed

name: SafeStage
evaluates: Unsafe success across the task lifecycle: hazards present in the initial state, during execution, and left in the final state
improves: Benchmarks do not check relation-dependent preconditions, execution-time interactions or post-completion physical states
setup: Isaac Sim (PhysX); simulated DROID setup with Franka Panda and Robotiq gripper
scale: 97 scenarios (27 initial-state, 40 execution-time, 30 final-state); 3 prompt conditions
policies: π0.5, GR00T N1.7, DreamZero, Cosmos3 Nano Policy without fine-tuning; aggregate success 33.74% but safe success 9.84%; about 71% of successful rollouts are unsafe
status: Code repository listed

name: OopsieVerse
evaluates: Damage caused during household manipulation: mechanical (impact, compression, tension), thermal and fluid damage measured by a simulator plugin
improves: Simulators do not detect or quantify the damage that unsafe interactions would cause
setup: DamageSim plugin on OmniGibson (BEHAVIOR-1K) and MuJoCo (RoboCasa); Franka Panda for real tests
scale: 32 tasks (21 unique designs across two simulators); 450 demonstrations for learning experiments
real_check: Shelving and pouring were run on a Franka Panda: damage-aware policies reached 65% safe completion vs 5% for the baseline; method transfer, damage agreement described qualitatively.
policies: GR00T: 8-92% completion but 0-8% safe completion on OmniGibson tasks; π0: 17.5% completion and 0% safe completion on RoboCasa tasks; imitation and RL baselines with health feedback also tested
status: Project site with code

name: ManiGuard-Bench
evaluates: Specification-grounded safety: LTLf spatial invariants and temporal ordering constraints monitored during contact-rich tabletop tasks, in- and out-of-distribution
improves: Manipulation benchmarks do not define or monitor safety during execution, and formal-specification benchmarks lack contact-rich trajectories and safety-annotated data
setup: Isaac Sim / OmniGibson (PhysX); BDDL predicates; Franka Panda
scale: 200 base tasks expanded to 1,000 scenarios (1 in-distribution and 4 shifted conditions each); 6 task families; 8,000 demonstrations
real_check: Three fine-tuned policies were run on a physical Franka on two task families (30 rollouts per cell); sim-real correlation is reported: r = 0.91 for success, 0.88 for safe success, 0.09 for violation rate.
policies: π0.5, π0, SmolVLA, GR00T N1.6; zero-shot safe success 0.0-1.8%, fine-tuned 7.5-29.8%; a large share of successful rollouts violate a specification
status: Project page, code and Hugging Face collection listed
note: The only entry in this slice with a numeric sim-real correlation.

name: BeSafe-Bench (BSB-EmbodiedVLA)
evaluates: Operational safety of a VLA during LIBERO manipulation, reported as success, safety and success-and-safe rates
improves: Agent-safety benchmarks rarely execute actions in functional environments, and embodied evaluation ignores behavioural safety
setup: LIBERO-90 tasks extended through VLA-Arena; 7-DoF arm
scale: One of four tracks in a 1,312-task agent-safety benchmark; the size of the VLA track was not extracted
policies: OpenVLA 49.81% success and 30% success-and-safe; OpenVLA-OFT 56.85% and 35.19%; π0.5 23.89% and 13.89%
status: No code or project URL found
note: Mainly a web, mobile and LLM-agent benchmark; the VLA track is a small part. The arXiv ID is 2603.25747 while the API lists a first-version date of 2026-01-30.

name: SoftVTBench
evaluates: Safe handling of deformable objects: a rollout counts as safe only without drops and with peak deformation below a calibrated threshold
improves: Success-only evaluation overstates performance because many goal-completing rollouts violate physical safety limits
setup: Isaac Sim 4.5.0 with PhysX 5 FEM soft bodies; Franka Panda with GelSight Mini tactile sensors
scale: 40 tasks in 4 matched suites; 2,000 demonstration episodes; 33 assets (19 rigid, 14 deformable)
policies: π0.5 vision-only: 70.4% goal success and 21.4% safety success on the soft-object suite; π0.5 visuo-tactile: 71.8% and 35.6%
status: Project page available; described as an early version
note: Venue from the arXiv comment ('Accepted by ECCVW').

name: WireCraft
evaluates: Industrial deformable-linear-object manipulation: connector insertion at a stated 3 mm plug–socket clearance, clip routing and channel seating, with reach success and insertion success reported separately
improves: Earlier cable and wire benchmarks did not align simulation tasks, real-robot data and one evaluation protocol across RL, imitation and VLA policies
setup: Isaac Lab 2.2.1 / Isaac Sim 4.5; four connector geometries (cylinder, cuboid, Ethernet, DisplayPort), 1–3 clip routing, straight and curved channel seating; two DLO physics models; shared policy interface
scale: 3 task families; 1,000 scripted trajectories for imitation / VLA training; about 150,000 scripted transitions for state-based RL
real_check: UR5 Ethernet insertion with ACT trained on mixed real and simulated data reached 4/10 insertions; no sim–real correlation statistic is reported.
policies: Ethernet insertion: π0.5 6.2% reach / 0.0% insertion; a Diffusion Transformer VLA policy 3.13% insertion; state PPO 95.86% insertion for comparison
status: New (June 2026); authors state benchmark, data and tools will be released on acceptance; no leaderboard
note: Numbers read from the arXiv HTML v1. ACT and Diffusion Policy values are given only in a figure, so they are not quoted here.

name: Bench2Dex
evaluates: Bimanual manipulation with multi-fingered hands across 12 arm–hand embodiments: tool use, articulated objects, jigsaw assembly, piano keys, pouring and box loading, with a shared tactile image for finger contact
improves: Dexterous-hand benchmarks were tied to one hand and had no common tactile observation format, so policies could not be compared across hand morphologies
setup: NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim; 12 dexterous hands; standardized tactile interface that ray-casts contact distance into 8-bit images; seven perturbation factors split into invariance and equivariance groups
scale: 26 bimanual tasks; about 1,300 human-teleoperated demonstrations (Manus glove + ARKit); 20,800 evaluation rollouts, 50 per task–embodiment–channel
policies: Matched scenes, 1,300 rollouts each: GR00T N1.5 48.5%, ACT 29.5%, π0.5 27.3%, Diffusion Policy 12.9%. Combined perturbations: GR00T N1.5 19.8%, π0.5 19.7%, ACT 13.0%, Diffusion Policy 3.8%
status: New technical report (September 2026); code and data on GitHub, Hugging Face and ModelScope; no public leaderboard found
note: Simulation only; hand and tactile models are not calibrated against hardware. Most tasks are loading, sorting or pouring, so the precision demand is finger coordination rather than tight clearance. The project page quotes 25.5% for π0.5 under shift; the paper table gives 19.7%.

name: SurgVLA-Bench
evaluates: VLA control of laparoscopic instruments under an endoscopic view: needle and gauze picking, electrocoagulation, vessel clipping and hemostasis, where small positioning errors on thin objects fail the task
improves: VLA models had no surgical evaluation with a task hierarchy from atomic actions to full procedures
setup: SurRoL (PyBullet) with added organ models; 8 tasks in three levels (atomic, conditional with distractors, composite); step limits of 100–150
scale: 8 tasks; over 800 simulated trajectories (about 40,000 frames) for LoRA fine-tuning; 50 trials per model per task
policies: OpenVLA 36–76% on Level 1 and 0% on Level 3; π0 0–76% on Level 1; π0.5 0–78% on Level 1 and 0–12% on Level 3; SmolVLA 0–8% on all levels
status: New (June 2026); code and data on GitHub; no leaderboard
note: Ranges are per-task spans read from Table 2 via the arXiv HTML; success is binary and no positional-error metric is reported. Simulation only.

name: UniVTAC Benchmark
evaluates: Visuo-tactile gripper manipulation on eight tasks, four of them contact-rich insertions or extractions (hole, HDMI, tube, key) where alignment must be corrected from fingertip contact
improves: Tactile policy learning lacked a simulator that both generates large tactile datasets and gives a common benchmark for visuo-tactile policies
setup: TacEx on NVIDIA Isaac Sim with IPC soft-body contact; simulated GelSight Mini, ViTai GF225 and Xense WS sensors; automated data generation
scale: 8 tasks; 50 demonstrations per task; 100 evaluation rollouts per task
real_check: Three real tasks (Insert Tube, Insert USB, Bottle Upright) on a Tianji Marvin arm: 43.3% vision-only versus 68.3% with the simulation-pretrained tactile encoder; no sim–real correlation statistic.
policies: Not in the benchmark paper. The later N0-VTLA paper reports 83.1% mean on the eight tasks for N0-VTLA and 67.1% for the strongest baseline, InternVLA-A1
status: Released February 2026 with project page; paper baselines are ACT, VITaL and ACT + UniVTAC encoder (30.9%, 40.5%, 48.0% average); reused by N0-VTLA and NeoSim (2026)
note: No stated insertion clearance was confirmed. VLA numbers come from a different paper (arXiv 2607.23782), not from the benchmark authors.

name: DexHoldem
evaluates: Real ShadowHand-on-UR-arm handling of thin playing cards (about 0.3 mm) and chips over 14 primitives: pickup, placement, revealing, chip moves; scores task completion and scene-preserving success
improves: Dexterous-hand benchmarks and embodied-agent benchmarks were separate; none required perception, game-state tracking and multi-fingered control together in a real scene that each action changes
setup: ShadowHand mounted on a UR arm at a physical Texas Hold'em table; 14 manipulation primitives; separate policy, perception (VLM) and closed-loop system benchmarks
scale: 14 primitives; 1,470 teleoperated demonstrations (105 per primitive); 80 trials per policy, 720 policy trials in total; 33 closed-loop hands
policies: Task completion / scene-preserving success: π0.5 61.2% / 47.5%, π0 57.5% / 47.5%, RDT 46.2% / 30.0%, Diffusion Policy (DINO) 36.2% / 26.2%; ACT, BAKU and other DP variants 1.2–20.0%. Full-hand completion 12.1%
status: Preprint (v3, October 2026); dataset on Hugging Face and code on GitHub; single-lab hardware, no leaderboard
note: Numbers from arXiv HTML v3. Requires a ShadowHand, so reproduction by other labs is costly; arXiv listing title of an earlier version differs ('Playing Texas Hold'em with Dexterous Embodied System').

name: MetaFine
evaluates: Fine-grained manipulation split into understanding, perception and behaviour; reports stage-wise success for 10 atomic skills including Align and Insert under position and angle tolerances, plus trajectory smoothness
improves: Binary task success hides which sub-skill fails; the authors report up to 70% capability inflation when only binary success is used
setup: Simulation tasks rebuilt from RoboTwin, CALVIN and LIBERO into one skill-graph format; 431 objects with 1,078 labelled parts; perturbation levels for viewpoint and lighting
scale: 10 atomic skills; 45+ task instances; 100 demonstrations per task; 7 policies
real_check: 20–25 paired real rollouts per policy are combined with simulation through prediction-powered inference, cutting estimate variance (11.5% to 2.6% for π0.5); no correlation coefficient is reported.
policies: ACT, DP3, Octo, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, π0, π0.5 evaluated. Peg-in-hole Align stage: Octo 4%, OpenVLA-OFT 19%, π0.5 0% (32% after a visual-encoder change). Part-substitution instructions drop all five VLAs to 0%
status: New (May 2026); code on GitHub, data on Hugging Face; no leaderboard
note: Per-skill numbers were read through an automated summary of the arXiv HTML and should be checked against the paper tables before quoting.

name: WorkBenchMark
evaluates: End-to-end assembly of LEGO Duplo structures from scattered bricks; interlocking studs require aligned placement and full press-down, scored by assembly success and per-connection execution accuracy
improves: Assembly benchmarks lacked a graded complexity scale tied to RoboCup Smart Manufacturing League tasks that both planning pipelines and end-to-end VLAs can be run on
setup: MuJoCo via LIBERO for simulation; UR5 with wrist RGB-D camera for the real subset; four tiers from two-brick stacks to interlocking 3–12 brick structures
scale: 400 simulation tasks (100 per tier); real subset of 10 tasks per tier
real_check: The planning pipeline was run on a UR5 for Tiers 1–3 (90%, 90%, 70% success); the VLA baseline was not run on the real robot and no sim–real correlation is reported.
policies: Fine-tuned π0.5 success by tier 1–4: 82%, 63%, 23%, 2%; zero-shot Gemini 2.5 Flash + π0.5: 70%, 59%, 19%, 5%; planning pipeline: 94%, 87%, 67%, 62%
status: New (June 2026); project page; tied to the RoboCup Smart Manufacturing League; no leaderboard
note: Duplo bricks are mechanically forgiving (the authors say so), so the precision demand is alignment to the stud grid rather than tight clearance.

name: ForceBench
evaluates: How a six-axis wrist force signal should be fed to a VLA, on eight tasks covering physical-property inference, resistance-dependent interaction (faucets, stove knobs, drawer) and contact-rich assembly (nut threading)
improves: Force-aware VLA papers each used their own tasks and fusion design, so force-integration strategies had not been compared under one protocol
setup: Simulation at 60 Hz physics / 15 Hz control with a π0.5 backbone and six force-fusion variants; separate real evaluation on a Franka Research 3 with KWR75B force/torque sensor and Robotiq gripper
scale: 8 simulation tasks; 1,600 demonstrations (200 per task); 16,000 simulation episodes; 800 real trials on 5 real tasks (20 per task–system pair)
real_check: Five separately trained real tasks (Weight Sort, Plate Retrieve, Stamp Press, Plug Insert, Block Insert): π0.5 without force 40%, best force variants 63%; this is not sim-to-real transfer and no correlation is reported.
policies: Simulation average over 8 tasks: π0.5 without force 23.25%, π0.5 with prompt-fusion force 35.31%; π0, ForceVLA and ForceFlow included as reference models
status: Project page only as of 2026-10; paper, code and data links not yet active
note: Verified from the project page only; no arXiv paper was found, and the simulator name is not stated on the page. Treat all numbers as preliminary.

name: Tabero
evaluates: Force-controlled grasping in LIBERO tasks replayed with simulated GelSight sensors; besides success it reports average and peak grip force and applied force under 'gentle' versus 'firm' instructions
improves: VLA benchmarks score only task success and carry no tactile signal, so they cannot tell whether a policy handled an object with appropriate force
setup: Isaac Lab 2.2+ / Isaac Sim 5.0+ with Taxim / FOTS tactile simulation; LIBERO trajectories regenerated with tactile images, marker fields and force; hybrid force–position control interface
scale: LIBERO-derived task set; the reported evaluation uses 9 tasks and 450 trials; three datasets with different force levels
policies: Tabero-VTLA (π0 with LoRA and tactile inputs): 86% success at 32.4 N average grip force under firm instructions; 52% success at 3.7 N under gentle instructions
status: New (May 2026); code and weights released; no leaderboard; no third-party results found
note: Measures force precision rather than positional precision. The total number of tasks in the full benchmark was not confirmed; only the authors' own model is reported.

name: ManiFeel
evaluates: Visuotactile imitation policies on insertion (peg, USB, power plug, gear), screwing (nut–bolt, bulb) and exploration tasks, comparing vision-only, tactile-RGB and tactile force-field inputs
improves: No reproducible simulation benchmark existed for supervised visuotactile policy learning across sensing modalities and policy architectures
setup: IsaacGym with TacSL tactile simulation; Franka Panda with GelSight R1.5 sensor; Diffusion Policy, Equivariant Diffusion Policy and Flow Matching baselines
scale: 99 simulation setups and 44 real setups; 20–100 teleoperated demonstrations per task; about 1,500 simulation rollouts per setup; 15 real rollouts per configuration
real_check: Gear assembly, bulb installation and ball sorting were repeated on a real Franka; the authors state the simulation trends were reproduced, without a correlation statistic.
status: Code, data and checkpoints released; the project page lists a Best Paper Award at the Sense of Space workshop, CVPR 2026; no VLA baseline
note: No stated clearances were found. Task counts differ between the project page (11 tasks listed) and the paper summary (99 setups); the main publication venue was not confirmed.

name: PRISM
evaluates: Real industrial contact-rich skills with force/torque and visuotactile sensing: connector plug/unplug, bearing installation, NIST task-board operations, caliper packaging, conveyor sorting; baseline protocol reports success on three tasks
improves: Large robot datasets focus on short, low-contact pick-and-place and lack synchronized force, tactile and multi-view data for tight-tolerance industrial procedures
setup: Franka Panda, bimanual Realman RM75-6F and LEJU humanoid; parallel, visuotactile and dexterous-hand end-effectors; multi-view RGB-D, 6-axis F/T at 100 Hz, visuotactile images; baseline evaluation on the Realman platform
scale: 25 tasks; 5,000+ teleoperated trajectories (about 45 hours) with paired human demonstrations; baselines use 200 demonstrations per task and 20 trials per configuration
policies: With pretraining, 200 demos: plug/unplug ACT 10%, Diffusion Policy 10%, π0 25%; caliper packaging 55%, 55%, 85%; conveyor sorting 30%, 20%, 85%
status: Dataset and project page released; primarily a dataset with a three-task baseline protocol; no leaderboard
note: IROS 2026 venue is taken from the GitHub repository title, not the arXiv page. Tolerances are described as tight but not given in millimetres.

name: NeoSim
venue: arXiv 2026-07 (introduced in the N0-VTLA / N0-Foundation reports)
evaluates: Visuo-tactile gripper manipulation on 12 tasks (4 single-arm, 8 dual-arm): charger and USB plugging, screw insertion, gear placement, chip grasping, pouring, handover, stacking and unstacking
improves: Tactile VLA models had no simulation suite whose contact force fields match the format of the real sensor used for training, so sim and real tactile results were not comparable
setup: Built in the UniVTAC framework (Isaac Sim); renders per-contact three-axis force fields in the NeoForce sensor format; fixed language prompt per task
scale: 12 tasks; 100 demonstrations per task for training
real_check: A companion real suite, NeoReal (9–10 contact-rich tasks), reports π0.5 29.4% versus N0-VTLA 47.2%; no sim–real correlation is reported.
policies: Mean success: N0-VTLA 50.8%, π0.5 45.8%, Xiaomi-Robotics-0 23.4%, StarVLA-alpha 23.2%, GigaWorld-Policy 10.8%, InternVLA-A1 8.6%; LingBot-VA 32.1% in the companion data report
status: New (July 2026); introduced inside a model paper by NeoteAI and Fudan; code repositories linked; no leaderboard or third-party use found
note: Benchmark is described in a method paper and a company report; number of evaluation trials and whether the task assets are public were not confirmed. NeoReal task count differs between the two reports (9 vs 10).

name: FACT contact-rich task suite
evaluates: Five real contact-rich tasks for VLAs with a wrist force/torque sensor: plug, USB and key insertion needing sub-millimetre alignment under occlusion, button push to a force threshold, whiteboard erasing
improves: VLA failures in contact-rich tasks were reported as one number; this study separates precision failures from force failures and compares force-aware VLAs on the same tasks
setup: Franka Research 3 with Bota SensONE 6-axis F/T sensor (400 Hz), external and wrist cameras at 15 Hz; π0.5 fine-tuned with LoRA; fixtures described by a bill of materials and 3D-printable files
scale: 5 tasks; 40 rollouts per task and method; nearly 2,500 real rollouts in total
policies: Average over five tasks: FACT (π0.5 backbone) 66%; best prior baseline ForceVLA 40.5%; π0.5 and TA-VLA also compared. FACT per task: plug 57.5%, USB 47.5%, key 60%, button 75%, board 90%
status: New (August 2026); task suite sits inside a method paper from Stanford IPRL; hardware files and code announced, availability not confirmed
note: Not presented as a benchmark by its authors. Per-baseline numbers other than the ForceVLA average were not extracted.

name: DexToolBench
evaluates: Real multi-fingered tool use: grasping a tool, rotating it in hand by 90 degrees and using it (hammer swing, marker writing, screwdriver spin, brush, eraser, spatula), scored by fraction of goal poses tracked
improves: Dexterous tool-use results were reported per tool with task-specific policies; no shared real-world task set with matching simulation environments existed
setup: 7-DoF KUKA iiwa 14 with 22-DoF Sharpa five-fingered hand; 6 tool categories, 12 object instances; digital-twin simulation environments and purchase links for the objects
scale: 24 tasks; 5 real rollouts per task, 120 rollouts in total
status: Released with project page (simtoolreal.github.io); baselines are kinematic retargeting, fixed grasp and specialist RL policies; no VLA or generalist-policy result found
note: Benchmark is defined inside a method paper. Needs a Sharpa hand and KUKA arm, which limits reproduction.

name: DexCraft
evaluates: Articulated tool use with a multi-fingered hand: hold the tool at a goal pose and actuate its joint with a finger (spray trigger, lighter lid, pump, pliers, stapler, pen click)
