improves: Dexterous-hand suites centre on grasping and relocation; these tasks need a stable grasp and an independent finger motion at once, which parallel grippers cannot do
setup: ManiSkill3; xArm6 with 16-DoF LEAP Hand (22-dimensional action); success requires tool pose match and joint triggered beyond a threshold
scale: 6 tasks; 5 teleoperated demonstrations per task expanded to 100 with MimicGen
real_check: Three real tasks (syringe, spray bottle, scissors), 50 demonstrations and 18 episodes: 40.7% for the proposed method versus 7.4% for DP3; these are different tasks, so no sim–real correlation.
status: New (June 2026); baselines are Diffusion Policy, DP3 and hierarchical variants (DP3 19.1%, proposed method 64.6%); no VLA baseline
note: Benchmark is defined inside a method paper from CMU; the RSS venue was reported by an automated summary and is not confirmed.

name: AutoMate
evaluates: Plug-into-socket assembly over 100 part geometries with contact-rich insertion; specialist and generalist policies are scored by success per assembly in simulation and on a real robot
improves: Earlier assembly simulation work (Factory, IndustReal) covered a handful of part types; no large, simulation-ready and 3D-printable set of assemblies existed for training and comparing policies
setup: Isaac Gym environments (also integrated into Isaac Lab); 100 assemblies that are both simulation-compatible and 3D-printable
scale: 100 assemblies; real evaluation of 200 policy-only trials over 20 assemblies and 100 perception-initialized trials over 5 assemblies
real_check: Zero-shot sim-to-real: about 80% success in simulation and 86–90% mean in perception-initialized real trials; the authors report real performance similar to or better than simulation.
status: Environments shipped in IsaacGymEnvs and Isaac Lab; used as an RL assembly test bed; no VLA result found
note: Clearances are not stated on the pages opened. Baselines are RL specialists and a distilled generalist, not VLAs.

name: QBIT
evaluates: Peg-in-hole and USB insertion quality at 1 mm and 0.1 mm clearance, measured by success, completion time, force energy, force smoothness and peak contact force
improves: Insertion benchmarks reported success rate only; contact quality and the effect of randomized contact parameters on sim-to-real transfer were not measured
setup: MuJoCo with randomized stiffness, damping and friction, run at scale on Kubernetes with ROS 2 containers; real UR5e with SCHUNK FTN-AXIA80 force/torque sensor
scale: 100 real repetitions per method; over 1,000 simulation runs per randomization study; three methods compared
real_check: The same three insertion methods were run on a real UR5e; the paper compares mesh-decomposition choices by how closely simulated contact matches the real robot, without a correlation statistic.
status: Code on GitHub; no public submission portal found; baselines are position control, impedance control and InsertionNet; no VLA result
note: Listed as submitted to IEEE; final venue not confirmed. One of the few insertion benchmarks with force-quality metrics.

name: VTDexManip
evaluates: Multi-fingered manipulation with vision and binary tactile input on six tasks: bottle-cap turning, faucet screwing, lever sliding, table and in-hand reorientation, bimanual hand-over
improves: No visual-tactile dataset and benchmark existed for pretraining and comparing representations on complex dexterous-hand skills
setup: IsaacGym; multi-finger hand; human visual-tactile dataset for pretraining; RL policy learning on top of 18 pretrained and non-pretrained encoders
scale: 6 tasks; 182 objects in the dataset; 18 methods compared
status: Code and dataset on GitHub; RL benchmark with no VLA or imitation baseline
note: Details were read from the GitHub README and search summaries of the ICLR paper; the paper PDF was not parsed and no arXiv abs URL was found, so the Paper link points to the ICLR proceedings PDF.

name: RoboPianist
evaluates: Piano playing with two 24-DoF Shadow hands; each key must be pressed at the right time, scored by precision, recall and F1 of key presses against the MIDI score
improves: Dexterous-hand benchmarks lacked a task with high-dimensional control, strict spatial and temporal precision and an interpretable continuous metric
setup: MuJoCo; two Shadow Dexterous Hands over a simulated piano; MIDI pieces with fingering annotations
scale: 150 pieces (Repertoire-150), with a 12-piece Etude-12 subset; RL baseline reaches F1 0.79 on Etude-12
status: Open-source environment used in dexterous RL work; no VLA result found
note: Uses state-based RL with task-specific rewards; it has no language-conditioned or image-based protocol, so VLA evaluation would need an adapter.

name: RTC Kinetix dynamic benchmark
evaluates: Solve rate of action-chunking policies on 12 force-controlled dynamic tasks (throwing, catching, balancing) as inference delay d (0-4 control steps) and execution horizon s are swept
improves: Common imitation-learning simulators are quasi-static, so long open-loop chunks reach near-perfect success and hide the cost of inference delay
setup: Kinetix 2D physics simulator (JAX), force-based control with Gaussian action noise; the world keeps stepping during the simulated inference delay, so there is no way to hold position while waiting
scale: 12 environments (10 existing Kinetix levels + 2 new); 1M-transition dataset per environment from RPO experts; 2,048 rollouts per data point
real_check: The same paper runs 6 real bimanual tasks with π0.5 under +0/+100/+200 ms injected latency (480 episodes, 28 h), but no sim-real correlation is reported.
policies: No VLA runs on the simulator itself (policies are small MLP-Mixer flow policies). Original comparison: RTC, BID, temporal ensembling, naive async. Later reported on by training-time RTC, VLASH, A2C2, FASTER, DEFLECT, DSDyn-VLA, Real-Time EXPO-FT and others
status: De facto standard delay benchmark for real-time chunking work (at least 14 follow-up papers opened in this search use it); MIT-licensed code, no leaderboard
note: Tasks are abstract 2D rigid-body levels, not robot-arm manipulation, and there is no language or vision input. Delay is a fixed number of control steps, not measured wall-clock latency.

name: RTC real-world latency protocol (injected delay)
evaluates: Sub-step score and throughput (task fraction completed per unit time) on six bimanual tasks at 50 Hz control with +0, +100 and +200 ms injected inference latency
improves: Real-robot VLA evaluations normally run one latency setting and report success only, so they cannot show how performance and speed degrade as inference gets slower
setup: Bimanual robot with two 6-DoF arms and parallel grippers (two tasks on a mobile base), π0.5 with 50-step chunks at 20 ms; real world, so the scene keeps evolving during inference
scale: 6 tasks (light candle with a match, plug ethernet, make bed, shirt folding, batch folding, dishes in sink); 10 trials per task per method per delay; 480 episodes, 28 h
policies: π0.5 with RTC shows no throughput loss up to +200 ms; synchronous inference degrades linearly with delay; both temporal-ensembling variants trigger protective stops at +100/+200 ms
status: Protocol described in the paper and reused in spirit by later work; tasks and hardware are Physical Intelligence internal, no shared task kit
note: Not a packaged benchmark: there is no released task set, so other labs can copy the delay-injection protocol but not the tasks. Throughput values are shown in a figure, not a table.

name: async-vla-inference (bt-kinetix / bt-libero)
evaluates: Success of four asynchronous-inference methods (inference-time RTC, training-time RTC, VLASH, A2C2) under inference delays up to 15 control steps on Kinetix and 20 steps on LIBERO
improves: The four methods had been evaluated in separate codebases with different base policies and delays of at most 4 steps (80 ms at 50 Hz)
setup: Kinetix (JAX, MLP-Mixer flow policies) and LIBERO (PyTorch/LeRobot, SmolVLA); delay injected as d control steps during which the previous chunk keeps executing
scale: 10 Kinetix environments, chunk sizes 16 and 30, 2,048 rollouts per configuration; 40 LIBERO tasks, 10 rollouts per task per delay, delays 0-20
policies: SmolVLA on LIBERO: inference-time RTC about 75% and A2C2 about 70% at d=0; A2C2 leads from d>=4. On Kinetix A2C2 stays above 90% solve rate up to d=8
status: Single-author bachelor-thesis preprint with public code; no leaderboard
note: LIBERO VLASH results use ground-truth future states, which the author flags as an upper bound. LIBERO scenes are quasi-static, so delay there affects only robot-state staleness.

name: DynaGrasp-32
evaluates: Success at intercepting and placing independently moving objects across six families: basic interception, object transfer, collision-induced path change, scene variation, multi-object sequencing, per-episode speed variation
improves: Lack of a common diagnostic suite for comparing heterogeneous frozen base VLAs on moving-object interception
setup: Isaac Sim, Franka Panda, three 256x256 RGB cameras, 30 Hz environment; the paper does not state whether simulation is paused during policy inference
scale: 32 tasks in 6 families; 50 closed-loop episodes per task (1,600 per model); DynaGrasp-1600 dataset of 1,600 teleoperated demonstrations, about 510K control steps
policies: Fine-tuned base VLAs: SmolVLA 62.50%, X-VLA 36.56%, π0 72.56%, π0.5 64.63%; with the DynaWM wrapper 69.69%, 81.88%, 74.44%, 75.56%
status: New; no code, dataset or project link in the paper
note: Object speeds in m/s were not found in the paper text. Coarse-tuned checkpoints of the same four VLAs score 37.69-48.44% (Table 2).

name: TIDAL Dynamic Interception (RoboCasa-GR1)
evaluates: Success at intercepting a target that moves with random 90-degree turns, placing it in a drawer and closing it, reported under both paused and non-paused physics at 50 Hz control
improves: Standard simulation pauses physics while the VLA computes, so replanning-heavy policies look good although their latency would make actions stale on a real robot
setup: RoboCasa GR-1 humanoid tabletop simulation; two protocols: paused (environment waits for inference) and non-paused (physics advances during inference, using Jetson AGX Orin latency figures)
scale: One task in Easy and Hard tiers; 2,000 fine-tuning episodes collected with a paused-simulation oracle
real_check: A real-robot rolling-target test over 100 trials is reported (motion-augmented open-loop baseline 34%, TIDAL roughly 2.5x); no sim-real correlation.
policies: GR00T N1.5 backbone, Easy tier: open-loop 0.31 paused vs 0.09 non-paused; compute-heavy replanning 0.63 vs 0.17; TIDAL 0.61 vs 0.30
status: Defined inside a method paper; no code or task release found
note: Unnamed suite; the label is descriptive. Rollout counts per cell for the simulation table were not found in the text.

name: AHEAD dynamic scenario suite
evaluates: Success on 20 moving-object scenarios (conveyor, beam, pole push, rolling ball, air hockey, ballistic catch, pinball deflection, plinko) with conveyor speed swept from 0 to 40 cm/s
improves: VLA evaluation assumes the scene is stationary between observation and execution; these scenarios make latency exceed the time available to grasp
setup: Custom MuJoCo environments with a Franka Panda, procedurally randomized object positions, motion parameters and lighting; the paper does not state how simulation time is coupled to inference time
scale: 20 scenarios in four motion categories; 5 training seeds x 100 rollouts per cell; five matching real tasks on a UFactory xArm 7 with 30 attempts each
real_check: Five real xArm 7 tasks: 29/30-30/30 on conveyor and rolling ball, 23/30 paddle interception, 19/30 projectile catching; sim-real gap discussed per task, no correlation statistic.
policies: Frozen 7B OpenVLA: open-loop about 0%, with fast replanning 16-33% on constant-velocity scenes, with the AHEAD world-model wrapper 79-97% versus 31-58% for the strongest baseline per scenario group
status: Defined inside a method paper; no code or environment release found in the PDF
note: Unnamed suite; the label is descriptive. Baseline figures are read from flattened tables and should be rechecked before quoting.

name: Robot Air Hockey Challenge
venue: NeurIPS 2023 competition (retrospective: NeurIPS 2024 D&B); second edition with IROS 2025 workshop
evaluates: Hit, defend and prepare sub-tasks and full games against an opponent with a fast puck, scored on success and a deployability penalty that includes per-step computation time under 0.02 s
improves: Real-world robot learning benchmarks assume quasi-static motion and do not penalise unsafe or too-slow controllers
setup: MuJoCo-based simulation of two KUKA LBR iiwa 14 arms on an air hockey table (1000 Hz simulation, 50 Hz control), then the top teams deployed on the real table
scale: 2023 qualifying stage: 1,000 episodes per sub-task; tournament: 15-minute games (45,000 steps); real-robot stage for the top three teams (top four in 2025)
real_check: In 2023 the top three solutions were run on the real two-arm platform; all performed considerably worse than in simulation and needed extra safety layers and hand tuning.
status: Two editions (2023, 2025); public code and documentation; leaderboard on the challenge site
note: The task is striking with a mallet, not grasping; entrants were RL and optimal-control agents with state input, and no VLA result was found. 2025 final results were not found on the pages opened. A separate retrospective says the 2023 ranking relied only on the simulated tasks.

name: Robot Air Hockey testbed
evaluates: Reaching, striking, juggling and puck-to-target tasks with a fast puck, using behaviour cloning, offline RL and RL from scratch at roughly 20 Hz
improves: Manipulation testbeds are dominated by quasi-static pick-and-place; policies that rely on slow robot motion are not exposed to fast object dynamics
setup: UR5 arm with a paddle on a small air hockey table and a 60 Hz overhead camera, plus Box2D and robosuite (MuJoCo) simulators of the same domain
scale: 10 tasks in Box2D, 6 in robosuite, 5 on the real robot; teleoperated human demonstration dataset
status: Research testbed with a project page; adoption beyond the authors not verified
note: Baselines are state- or puck-detection-based BC and RL policies, not VLAs. Publication venue was not confirmed (arXiv listing shows no venue).

name: HRIBench
evaluates: Collaboration success, completion time, temporal synchronization, response latency and safety when a scripted human instructs, hands over to, or interrupts the robot mid-task
improves: VLA benchmarks evaluate a robot acting alone and leave timing relative to a moving human, and recovery after human interference, unmeasured
setup: Simulated Franka Panda with a scripted human agent whose timing and motion vary per episode; the simulator and its coupling to inference time are not stated in the main text
scale: 13 role-conditioned tasks (Instructor, Collaborator, Intruder), over 650 evaluation episodes; 50 training and 10 held-out trajectories per task
real_check: A small real-robot study (3 tasks, 10 trials each) shows adding HRIBench data raises GR00T N1.5 success from 0.10 to 0.43; no sim-real correlation is reported.
policies: GR00T N1.5-LoRA, π0.5-LoRA and ACT: best collaboration success 0.533 on Instructor, 0.500 on Collaborator and 0.100 on Intruder tasks for all three policies
status: New preprint; no code link found in the PDF
note: Timing here means responding to human cues at the right moment, not control frequency; inference latency is not modelled.

name: Magiclab real-time VLA execution study
evaluates: Success, mean completion time, successful-task throughput per hour and action-continuity metrics for six real-time execution methods on bimanual garment folding, with measured end-to-end system latency
improves: Async execution methods were each tested on different robots and tasks, and robot-side delays (camera, communication, actuation) were not measured alongside model latency
setup: Bimanual physical robot running π0.5 with separate inference (1-3 Hz), action-publication (30-50 Hz) and control rates; latency calibrated with a visual time code and 100 Hz state logging
scale: 1 long-horizon task, 3 garments, 6 methods, 10 trials per garment per method (180 physical trials)
policies: π0.5 base: Legato 29/30 (73.6 s, 47.3 tasks/h); VLASH 28/30 (43.2/h); temporal smoothing 23/30 (29.4/h); training-time RTC and naive async 19/30; inference-time RTC no higher than 63.3%
status: New preprint with open-source framework; single lab, single task
note: Garment folding is not a moving-target task; the timing demand comes from asynchronous execution and throughput scoring. Trials are unpaired and the authors run no significance tests.

name: DynamicManip Benchmark
evaluates: Success and end-to-end policy-query latency on five moving-target tasks (tapping, belt picking, object catching, mole whacking, goal blocking), with the simulator advanced by the measured inference time before each action
improves: In conventional simulation inference time does not affect execution, so slow policies are not penalised on moving-object tasks
setup: RoboTwin 2.0 on SAPIEN with two ARX-X5 arms and a head camera; simulator steps forward round(t_infer / dt_sim) steps before each predicted action is applied, so the scene evolves during inference
scale: 5 simulated tasks with 200 expert demonstrations each, 100 evaluation trials per task; 4 real tasks with 50 demonstrations each on AgileX Piper arms, 30 trials per task
real_check: Four real tasks (dynamic tapping, belt picking, boat loading, bottle catching) on AgileX Piper arms are evaluated with 30 trials each; no sim-real correlation is reported.
status: Defined inside a method paper with a project page; code release not confirmed
note: Only point-cloud diffusion policies are evaluated (DP3: 20-78% success at 44-61 ms; the authors' policy: 42-88% at 31-38 ms); no VLA baseline. Object speeds are not stated in the text read.

name: RADAR
evaluates: VLA generalization on a physical arm under changes in lighting, background and sensor noise, across block-placement and spatial-reasoning task splits
improves: Real-world VLA tests that are static, human-reset and human-judged; replaces binary manual scoring with 3D-IoU-based automatic success measurement and automatic scene reset
setup: Self-contained robot cell: collaborative arm (example given: UR5e with Robotiq 2F-85), wrist RealSense D435, two fixed RealSense D415 cameras for 3D reconstruction, actuated task platform on a mechanical stage for automatic reset; client-server-worker architecture separates policy submission from execution
scale: 4 task splits (SingleBlock, TwoBlock, ThreeBlock, Spatial), 32 trials per model; 5 policies (π0, π0-FAST, π0.5, RDT, OpenVLA); best π0.5 17/32, π0 and π0-FAST 2/32, RDT and OpenVLA 0/32
note: No project page, code or public submission endpoint was found, so whether outside groups can submit is unverified; grouped as hosted because of the submission architecture.

name: LabDex
evaluates: Dexterous-hand manipulation of chemistry-laboratory objects at three levels: atomic skills, compositional skills and a long-horizon laboratory workflow
improves: Lack of a real-world dexterous benchmark for laboratory automation with shared task definitions across real and simulated platforms
setup: Franka Research 3 with XHand, three RealSense D435i cameras (wrist, left-front, head); teleoperation with Manus Quantum glove and VIVE tracker; matched simulation platform under the same task definitions
scale: 7 atomic-skill categories instantiated as 30+ atomic skills over 20+ objects, 10+ compositional skills, 1 long-horizon workflow; 200 demonstrations per task by default; 26 atomic skill instances evaluated with 50 real trials each; overall average π0.5 0.57, ACT 0.34, DP 0.02
note: Dataset homepage is named in the paper but release status of code and data was not checked.

name: CEBench
evaluates: Cross-embodiment practicality of VLA models on single-arm (CALVIN), bimanual (RoboTwin) and a real bimanual mobile robot, with and without domain randomization
improves: VLA evaluations that cover one embodiment at a time and omit domain-randomized real-world tests
setup: Real part: Cobot-Magic dual-arm mobile robot with Piper arms; 8 fixed-base tasks and 2 mobile manipulation tasks; domain randomization over color/texture, distractors and workspace layout. Simulation part: CALVIN and RoboTwin
scale: 1.6k real expert trajectories (200 per fixed-base task); 100 evaluation episodes per fixed-base task, 10 per mobile task; LLaVA-VLA 44.2% seen, 30.7% domain-randomized
note: Benchmark is introduced inside a method paper (LLaVA-VLA). Release of the real-world dataset was promised upon acceptance and not checked.

name: RoboChess Challenge
evaluates: Single-arm policies that perceive a chess board, choose legal moves and move physical chess pieces, in GPU-accelerated simulators and on real robots
setup: Simulation track (MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, Genesis) and real-world track (LeRobot SO-101, Franka, UR, Piper, Yam/Rebot); baselines include pi, GR00T and Cosmos-based policies; hosted by the CoRL 2026 Workshop on GPU-Accelerated Simulation to Scalable and Generalizable Robot Policy Learning
scale: Two tracks; winners to be announced 9 November 2026 in Austin; team count not stated
note: Workshop page opened. Submission deadline is a placeholder and the page does not say who runs the real robots or how real-track runs are scored.

name: SutureBot
evaluates: End-to-end autonomous suturing on a surgical robot: needle pickup, tissue insertion with pull-through, and knot tying, scored by success, insertion-point error and time
improves: No repeatable physical benchmark existed for long-horizon, millimetre-precision surgical manipulation by imitation-learning and VLA policies
setup: Da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) Si with DeBakey forceps and large needle driver, wrist cameras; insertion and exit error measured with UV markers; dataset and fixture STL files released
scale: 1,890 demonstrations (628 needle pickup, 310 needle throw, 952 knot tying; 454 recovery examples); 10 full suture procedures per policy; π0, GR00T N1, OpenVLA-OFT, multitask ACT; best 3/10 end-to-end
note: The arXiv comment gives NeurIPS 2025; the Datasets & Benchmarks track attribution comes from a third-party list and was not confirmed on the proceedings page.

name: HumanoidToolBench
evaluates: Humanoid tool use from choosing a suitable tool among candidates and decoys to using it while stationary or walking
improves: Existing benchmarks do not test tool selection, manipulation and locomotion jointly on a humanoid
setup: Unitree G1 with Dex3 hands and head camera in the real world; MuJoCo simulation counterpart; 55 tool assets; ToolBook demonstration dataset
scale: 18 tasks over 3 scenarios, 3 execution levels and 2 tool-set modes; 3,003 simulation and 91 real demonstrations; 7 policies in simulation, 3 on the real robot
note: Real-robot evaluation covers only a small subset of the tasks (level-1 ball tasks); most results are simulation.

name: TacO
evaluates: Which tactile sensor modality (resistive, magnetic, vision-based, acoustic) helps imitation-learned policies on pick-and-place with unknown mass, object reorientation and occluded plug insertion
improves: No empirical, task-driven comparison of tactile sensors under one hardware setup and policy pipeline
setup: Franka Panda arms with fin-ray fingers at two institutions over 2,000 miles apart; six sensors (FSR, FlexiTac, eGaIn, eFlesh, Daimon, contact microphone); ACT policies trained per sensor; open-source repeatability test kit
scale: 3 tasks; 50-60 demonstrations per task; examples: pick-and-place with FlexiTac 0.85 vs 0.75 vision-only; plug insertion 0.70 with contact microphone vs 0.2 vision-only
note: Benchmarks sensors rather than policies; release of hardware, code and data is promised on a project website whose URL was not found.

name: Eval-Actions
evaluates: Execution quality of real-robot manipulation episodes beyond binary success, using expert grades, rank-guided labels and diagnostic explanations, plus a learned evaluator (AutoEval) that predicts them
improves: Binary success rates hide process-level differences among executions that complete the same task; human grading does not scale
setup: Offline benchmark of teleoperated and policy-generated episodes on ARX R5 and UR5 arms (single-arm and bimanual) with RGB-D video and robot states; AutoEval takes RGB frames and kinematic summaries
scale: 13K+ episodes, 150+ tasks, about 52 hours; annotated subset 6K+ episodes over 50+ tasks; AutoEval-S Spearman 0.81 (expert grading) and 0.84 (rank-guided), success detection 90.6-91.0%
note: This is an evaluation-tooling entry: it scores recorded real episodes and does not run policies. Earlier title: 'Trustworthy Evaluation of Robotic Manipulation: A New Benchmark and AutoEval Methods'.

name: WorldComposer
evaluates: Manipulation policies in simulation scenes generated from real-world panoramas, plus edited 'digital cousin' scenes for unseen-scene and unseen-object generalization
improves: Building simulation evaluation scenes by hand is slow, and real-world generalization tests need new physical assets and room reconfiguration
setup: Panorama-to-scene generation (Marble) into NVIDIA Isaac Sim; validation on bimanual LeRobot SO-101 follower arms with a top-down RGB camera
scale: 3 tasks (Set Tableware, Open Microwave, Fold Cloth); 4 policies (ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA, π0); 4 generalization levels; 100 simulated and 20 real trials per configuration
agreement: Pearson r = 0.91 between simulated and real success rates
note: Code repository URL not confirmed.

name: TOTO (Train Offline, Test Online)
evaluates: Offline imitation and offline-RL policies and pretrained visual representations on scooping and pouring with unseen objects, positions and lighting
improves: Few labs own robots and every lab uses a different one; a shared remote robot plus a common offline dataset gives like-for-like comparison without hardware
setup: One Franka Emika Panda with a RealSense D435 at the organizers' lab; users train on the released dataset and submit policies via a form; an engineer supervises runs and returns video, reward and success rate (about 12 h turnaround)
scale: 2 tasks; 1,000-2,000 trajectories per task in the initial release; 18 trials per method for seen and for unseen locations (2 objects x 3 locations x 3 seeds); initial baselines from 5 institutions; later run as a NeurIPS 2023 competition
note: Whether the remote evaluation service is still accepting submissions in 2026 was not checked.

name: ABC-Sim / ABC-Eval (ABC stack)
evaluates: Behavior-cloning policy checkpoints (DiT and VLA) in MuJoCo tasks built to mirror real bimanual tasks, alongside a released set of scored real-world rollouts
improves: Real-world ablations of model and training choices are costly; groups without hardware cannot evaluate at all
setup: MuJoCo tasks with 400 hours of VR sim-teleoperation data co-trained with the real ABC-130K dataset; ABC-Eval releases about 100 hours of real policy rollouts with rubric scores; hardware design, training and simulation code announced as open-source
scale: 12 checkpoints compared on 3 tasks (bottles into bin, plates into dishrack, turning mugs upright), 50 trials per task; ABC-130K: 3,500 hours, 130K episodes, 195 tasks; ABC-Sim: 20 tasks
agreement: Pearson r = 0.85 for strict success (p = 4.2e-4, n = 12) and r = 0.91 for task progress (p = 5.0e-5, n = 12)
note: Correlation holds for policies co-trained with the sim data; release status not checked.

name: OSCAR
evaluates: DROID generalist policies from the RoboArena leaderboard by rolling them out in a skeleton-conditioned video world model that covers several robot embodiments
improves: Video world models used as evaluators follow actions imprecisely and are tied to one embodiment
setup: Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B fine-tuned on curated robot and egocentric human data with 2D kinematic-skeleton conditioning; rollouts start from recorded RoboArena first frames with estimated camera calibration
scale: 7 policies (π0-flow, π0-FAST, and five PaliGemma variants); 65 RoboArena sessions retained
agreement: Against the RoboArena ranking: Pearson r = 0.852, Spearman 0.750, MMRV 0.571 (skeleton conditioning)
note: The 65 sessions were hand-selected for good camera-calibration estimates, which may favour agreement.

name: ICRA 2026 AI for Robotic Surgery Competition
evaluates: Peg transfer on a surgical robot in two challenges: human teleoperation and autonomous execution by a learned or programmed algorithm
setup: Da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) on site at ICRA 2026, with AMBF simulation for preparation; autonomous entries interface through ROS 2; score is pegs transferred within the time limit
scale: 2-4 June 2026; 21 participants in real-dVRK teleoperation, 18 in simulated teleoperation, 5 teams registered for the autonomous challenge; EUR 2,100 total prizes
note: Competition page opened. Results of the autonomous challenge were not found on the page.

name: World Humanoid Robot Games (scenario events)
evaluates: Humanoid robots on scenario events such as factory material handling, medicine sorting and dispensing, and hotel-room cleaning, next to athletic events
setup: On-site events in Beijing with teams bringing their own humanoids; in 2026 fully autonomous runs earn full points in scenario events and teleoperated runs half
scale: 2025: 280 teams, 500+ robots, 26 events; 2026: 666 teams, 2,056 robots, 51 events of which 21 are scenario-based
note: Verified from Wikipedia and a Sixth Tone report only; official per-event rules and manipulation-event results were not found, and the 2025 autonomy rules are unverified.

name: Robocurve / Inspect Robots
evaluates: Frontier models (VLAs, LLM agents, coding agents) on physical arms and bimanual stations in tasks such as block stacking, Tower of Hanoi, Jenga and bimanual manipulation, graded with staged rubrics
improves: No continuous, independent, standardized real-world measurement of robot capability; published demos are cherry-picked
setup: Independent evaluator (Public Benefit Corporation, Y Combinator-backed) running its own robot stations, including I2RT YAM bimanual cells; commissioned evaluations under benchmarking agreements; open-source MIT framework Inspect Robots with adapters for YAM, Franka, SO-100/101, WidowX, Unitree G1 arms, AgiBot A2, ROS arms
scale: Results published as reports and per-trial result pages rather than one leaderboard; one commissioned study: 5 tasks x 2 policies (π0.5, MolmoAct2) x 20 real trials = 200 graded trials; USD 10M seed announced 14 September 2026
note: Company site, GitHub repository and a third-party paper that used its trials were opened. Individual evaluation reports were not opened, so per-report task counts and model lists are unverified.

name: Kaedim real-to-sim reconstruction study (yam-sim-harness)
evaluates: How object and scene reconstruction quality (metric-scale geometry, authored physics, scene splat) changes agreement between simulated and real scores of manipulation policies on one bimanual cell
improves: Real-to-sim evaluation pipelines leave object geometry and physics at generative or engine defaults without measuring the effect on sim-real agreement
setup: Two simulated twins of an I2RT YAM bimanual cell (authored vs default open-source recipe) scored against the same real trials, which were run and graded by the third-party evaluator Robocurve with staged rubrics; harness, per-trial scores, assets and scenes released
scale: 5 tasks x 2 policies (π0.5, MolmoAct2) = 10 cells; 20 trials per cell in each reconstruction; 200 paired real trials
agreement: Pearson r = 0.90 (authored reconstruction) vs 0.51 (default); mean score error 6.97 vs 17.54 percentage points
note: Authors work for Kaedim, which sells the authored asset pipeline and paid for the real trials; with ten cells the correlation difference is not statistically separated.

name: RoboART (Predictive Red Teaming)
evaluates: How much a visuomotor policy's success rate will drop under off-nominal lighting, distractors, backgrounds and object placement, predicted without running the robot
improves: Exposing a policy's vulnerabilities to environmental factors needs many hardware trials per condition
setup: Generative image editing alters nominal observations per environmental factor; a policy-specific anomaly detector on the edited observations predicts success; validated on visuomotor diffusion policies on real hardware
scale: 500+ hardware trials across 12 off-nominal conditions
agreement: Less than 0.19 average absolute difference between predicted and real success rates
note: Abstract page opened (Google DeepMind and Princeton). Robot platform, task count and any peer-reviewed venue were not checked.

name: GeniWorld
evaluates: Fine-tuned π0 policy checkpoints in a URDF-rendered, action-conditioned video world model, including scenes with visual distractors
improves: Action-conditioned world models used as evaluators lose action controllability and break down in out-of-distribution scenes
setup: Autoregressive video model conditioned on rendered robot motion; each rollout starts from the same first frame as the real trial; humans judge success and a VLM judges plausibility
scale: Real comparison over several manipulation tasks in in-domain and distractor settings; separate data-generation study with 4 tasks x 5 settings x 20 real trials
agreement: Scatter plot of real vs world-model success rates described as a strong positive correlation; no coefficient given in the text
note: Agreement is shown only as a figure; number of policies and tasks in the correlation study was not extracted.

name: BiAssemble real-world benchmark
evaluates: Bimanual geometric assembly: picking up two fragments of a broken object, aligning them and joining them into the original shape
improves: Broken parts differ every time an object breaks, so real-world results on fracture assembly cannot be compared across labs
setup: Object set of commercially available items (wine glass, plate, beer bottle, bowl, mug, teapot) with reproducible broken parts and scanned 3D meshes usable in simulation; two Franka Panda arms and an Azure Kinect
scale: Six object categories; real-robot results in the paper are mostly qualitative
note: The benchmark is one section of a method paper. How the broken parts are reproduced and how many objects are included were not extracted.

name: The Imitator Game (IG-10K, Imitator Arena)
evaluates: Whether a policy shown a human demonstration video reproduces the demonstrated intent as the robot's scene diverges from the demonstration across four levels, up to substituting a different object
improves: Learning-from-human-video evaluations test trajectory replay in near-identical scenes and do not separate motion copying from task understanding
setup: Real domain on a dual-arm Realman robot with ZED2i camera and a separate ManiSkill3 simulation domain; paired human-robot dataset; Imitator Arena gives automated scoring in simulation and blind A/B human rating of rollouts
scale: 20,000+ paired episodes, 50+ tasks, 6 domains; 10 evaluation tasks (5 seen, 5 unseen) at 4 levels; 9 models (15 trained variants); every model below 13% zero-shot success on unseen tasks
note: Number of real trials per task-level pair and public availability of the Arena were not extracted.

name: Perception Challenge for Bin-Picking (BPC)
evaluates: 6-DoF object pose estimation for industrial bin picking, judged in the final by whether a robot cell completes pick-and-place using the submitted estimates
setup: Organized by OpenCV with Intrinsic and partners; open industrial datasets for the first phase; real hardware made remotely usable through the Intrinsic platform, with finalists' code run on a real robot cell
scale: More than 450 teams; winners announced at CVPR 2025; prize pool reported as USD 60,000
note: Intrinsic blog post opened; the OpenCV results page returned HTTP 403, so the prize figure and phase structure come from search snippets. Entries are perception modules, not manipulation policies.

name: Food Topping Challenge (FTC)
evaluates: Robot handling of real food: serving salmon roe on rice bowls and picking pieces of fried chicken from a pile, scored on quantity and presentation
setup: On-site at ICRA 2024 in Yokohama, supported by a Robotics Society of Japan working group; teams bring their own approach, with the Foodly Type R dual-arm robot recommended
scale: Practice 14-15 May 2024, competition 16 May 2024; team count not found
note: ICRA 2024 competitions page and one participant paper abstract opened; the competition website no longer resolves, and whether later editions took place is unverified.

name: Robotic Sim2Real Challenge (AgileX Sim2Real / RMUS)
evaluates: Transfer of simulation-developed mobile manipulation to real robots: plate arranging with an AgileX mobile manipulator and mineral-cube search and grasping with a RoboMaster platform
setup: Organized by Tsinghua AIR at ICRA; teams develop in a provided simulator and their solutions are then run on the organizers' real robots; the 2025 edition kept a mobile manipulation track and added a flying-robot track
scale: Fourth edition at ICRA 2025; team counts not found
note: ICRA 2024 and ICRA 2025 competition pages opened; the challenge site sim2real.net refused connections, so stage structure and results are unverified.

name: Benjie's Humanoid Olympic Games
evaluates: Autonomous general-purpose mobile manipulators on household feats in five events: doors, laundry, tool use, fingertip manipulation and wet manipulation, each with bronze, silver and gold tasks
setup: Open, self-reported challenge posted by Benjie Holson: entrants submit an uncut 1x-speed video of an autonomous run; a robot may take up to 10x the author's own time; first to complete a task takes the medal, later claims must be 25% faster
scale: Round 1: 5 events x 3 medal tasks (15 tasks); Part II (27 January 2026) adds new events including eggs, tool use, bedroom skills, fingertip challenges and full body; first medal claimed by IHMC Robotics on 16 October 2025
note: Both Substack posts opened. Verification is by video only; the claim that Physical Intelligence completed 11 tasks within three months comes from press search snippets, not from the posts.

name: Robotic Construction Challenge (RCC)
evaluates: Autonomous identification, grasping and stacking of building blocks by one or two arms to reproduce a leaning tower (Abu Dhabi's Capital Gate) under construction rules
setup: Real robots only, for both practice and the on-site final; teams bring single- or dual-arm systems; each game lasts ten minutes and teams are ranked by points for placed blocks; organizers from Tsinghua, SYSU/MBZUAI, QIYUAN Lab, DISCOVER Robotics and RIT Dubai
scale: Practice 1 August - 14 October 2024, final 15-16 October 2024; awards for 16 ranked teams (USD 2,000 / 1,000 / 500 for the top three)
note: Competition page opened. Number of participating teams and winners were not on the page; described there as the first edition.

name: ASTM F45 mobile manipulator test method (WK92144)
evaluates: Positioning precision and accuracy of a mobile manipulator's arm and base on pose-constrained tasks such as tracing an S-shaped path and inserting pegs
improves: Lack of a quantifiable, reproducible in-situ test for mobile manipulator performance that vendors and users can share
setup: Standard test table developed from NIST research, built from low-cost components; the tabletop can lie flat, tilt to 45 degrees or stand vertical, with an optional shaker to add motion and vibration
scale: One apparatus with path-tracking and peg-insertion tasks; still under committee consensus when reported on 30 November 2024
note: Verified from a trade-press article only (the ASTM press release returned HTTP 403). The standard targets system accuracy rather than learned-policy evaluation, and its approval status in 2026 is unknown.

name: CT benchmark (human-robot collaborative assembly)
evaluates: Assembly of a standard model set performed manually, fully automatically and in human-robot collaboration, measured by assembly time and human workload (NASA-TLX)
improves: No shared, replicable model set for comparing human-robot collaborative assembly setups against manual and automatic baselines
setup: Physical model set whose components cover common assembly operations at several difficulty levels; three experimental setups (manual, automatic, collaborative)
scale: Collaborative assembly took 70.8% longer than manual assembly while lowering reported workload
note: Abstract page only was opened; robot hardware, number of parts and participant count were not extracted, and a journal version exists that was not opened.

name: RoboReward
evaluates: How well vision-language models assign end-of-episode progress scores (1-5) to real-robot rollout videos, and trained 4B/8B reward models for that purpose
improves: Human success labelling of real rollouts is slow, and it was unknown how reliable off-the-shelf VLMs are as automatic judges on real robot data
setup: Dataset and benchmark built from Open X-Embodiment and RoboArena real-robot videos, with negative and near-miss examples generated by counterfactual relabelling and temporal clipping; dataset, models and evaluation suite released
scale: Covers many tasks and embodiments from the two source corpora (exact counts not extracted); the 8B model was also used as the reward in real-robot reinforcement learning
note: Abstract page opened. Evaluation-tooling entry: it scores recorded real episodes and does not run policies. Dataset size and accuracy figures were not extracted.

name: FailBench
evaluates: Reliability of VLM-based judges at deciding whether a robot manipulation attempt succeeded, across many data sources
improves: VLM success detectors are adopted for evaluation with little evidence that they generalize across domains or handle naturally occurring failures
setup: Offline benchmark of manipulation attempts drawn from 14 public sources (12 real-world, 2 simulated); 75% of failures occur naturally; 13 VLM-based detectors compared by balanced accuracy
scale: 2,197 attempts; best detector 0.77 mean balanced accuracy; below 0.60 on contact-intensive assembly tasks
note: Abstract page only was opened; release location of the benchmark was not found. Evaluation-tooling entry that tests judges, not policies.

name: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5
evaluates: Manipulation rollouts at the process level: a process reward model turns rollout videos into progress curves, from which failure-side progress, recovery and success-side quality metrics are computed
improves: Binary success rates and hand-written stage scores do not show how far failed runs got or how cleanly successful runs were executed
setup: Open-source toolkit with metric implementations and visualization; applied to rollout videos from the RoboDojo real-world and simulation leaderboards; RoboPulse++ benchmark checks the process reward model on rollout intervals
scale: Applied to models on the RoboDojo leaderboard frozen on 3 July 2026; counts of videos and models not extracted
note: Evaluation-tooling entry; project URL and the accuracy of the process reward model were not extracted.

name: WEAVER
evaluates: Manipulation policies (base and fine-tuned π0.5) by rolling them out in a multi-view latent world model that also predicts reward, on long-horizon tasks lasting up to 40 seconds
improves: World models used as evaluators lack fidelity, long-horizon consistency or speed, and pretrained ones underestimate policy performance
setup: Multi-view world model trained with flow matching to predict future latents and reward; human-labelled success on imagined rollouts compared with real success rates averaged over 20 trials per task; compared with Ctrl-World
scale: Several real tasks including pouring and pick-and-place stacking; 20 real trials per task; exact task and policy counts not extracted
agreement: Pearson correlation 0.87 with real-world success rate after fine-tuning; higher correlation and lower MMRV than Ctrl-World
note: Policy evaluation is one of three applications in a method paper; MMRV values and the robot platform were not extracted.

name: Hi-WM
evaluates: Task success of generalist policies rolled out in closed loop inside an action-conditioned world model, used to decide where human corrections are needed
improves: Human-in-the-loop post-training and its evaluation both consume robot time, scene setup and resets
setup: Closed-loop policy rollouts in a learned world model with human intervention, rollback and branching; world-model success rates compared with real success rates on the same tasks
scale: 3 real-world tasks covering rigid and deformable objects; 2 policy backbones
agreement: Pearson r = 0.953 between world-model and real-world success rates
note: Evaluation is a sub-experiment of a post-training method paper; number of points in the correlation and the robot platform were not extracted.

name: Mem-World
evaluates: Manipulation policies in a memory-augmented multi-view world model built to stay consistent under end-effector occlusion and wrist-camera motion on long-horizon tasks
improves: World-model evaluators forget or hallucinate scene details over long rollouts, which degrades agreement on long-horizon tasks
setup: Multi-view action-conditioned video model with a wrist-view surfel-indexed memory; post-trained models are used for policy evaluation and compared with Ctrl-World
scale: 5 real tasks in the correlation study
agreement: Pearson r = 0.97 (p < 0.001) across five tasks, versus r = 0.85 for Ctrl-World; absolute success rates in the world model are lower than real
note: CoRL 2026 taken from the arXiv comment. Number of policies and the robot platform were not extracted.

name: RoboSnap / DROID-Sim
evaluates: Fine-tuned π0.5 policies in simulation scenes generated from a single RGB image of the real scene
improves: Building simulation scenes that are both physically stable and visually faithful is slow, which limits real-to-sim evaluation to a few hand-made scenes
setup: Layered real-to-sim: collision-aware foreground assets for interaction plus a 3D Gaussian splatting layer for background appearance; DROID-Sim companion dataset built from DROID scenes
scale: DROID-Sim: 564 real-world DROID scenes; correlation study on real-robot tasks with real-only fine-tuned π0.5 policies
agreement: Pearson r = 0.887 and MMRV 0.0066 between real and simulated success rates
note: Number of tasks and checkpoints in the correlation study was not extracted.

name: Agentic Real2Sim
evaluates: Manipulation policies in physics-simulation twins that VLM agents assemble automatically from real recordings of robot-object interaction
improves: Real-to-sim conversion needs manual tuning of perception tools, mesh cleanup and frame alignment for every scene
setup: VLM agents recover geometry, object states and physical parameters and build a runnable simulation episode; demonstrated on DROID episodes, deformable-object scenes and humanoid motion scenes
scale: Correlation study over 6 pick-and-place tasks
agreement: Pearson r = 0.920 (p = 0.009) between simulated and real task success rates
note: The correlation is across tasks rather than across policies; policy and trial counts were not extracted.

name: ViTacWorld
evaluates: Tactile manipulation policy checkpoints on contact-rich tasks by predicting both camera images and tactile feedback from robot actions
improves: Vision-only world models cannot roll out policies that need tactile input, and real tactile evaluation data are costly
setup: Action-conditioned visuo-tactile world model pretrained on public real tactile datasets and simulation, fine-tuned on real policy rollouts; imagined success compared with real success over 50 trials
scale: 12 task-checkpoint pairs; 50 trials each; tasks include cucumber peeling
agreement: Pearson r = 0.863, Spearman 0.790, mean absolute error 12.33 percentage points; underestimates success by 9.0 points on average
note: Authors state the results support relative comparison of the tested checkpoints only.

name: DexTouch-WM
evaluates: Dexterous-hand policies in a world model that jointly predicts RGB and full-hand tactile signals, trained with up to 100 hours of human touch data
improves: Tactile world models need dense robot tactile data that is costly to collect and tied to one sensor
setup: Piezoresistive tactile arrays with the same layout on human and robot hands; human motion retargeted to robot actions; imagined rollouts scored by five human raters and compared with real evaluation
scale: 4 tasks (place shoes, place phone, stack bowls, stand bottle); 5 hours of robot data plus 0-100 hours of human data
agreement: Per-task Pearson 0.972, 0.939, 0.889, 0.577 for the human+robot model (MMRV 0 to 0.067); 0.400 to 0.945 for the robot-only model
note: Workshop paper; correlations are computed over few policies per task.

name: HapticWorld
evaluates: Force-conditioned policies on contact-rich tasks inside a learned world simulator that predicts joint torque together with images
improves: Vision-only world simulators cannot run policies that take force or torque as input
setup: Interactive world model with real-time torque feedback to the teleoperator; in-simulator success rates compared with real success rates for policies trained on simulated and real data
scale: 3 contact-rich tasks (microwave opening, whiteboard wiping, box flipping); 20 real trials per task and configuration
agreement: Reported qualitatively: in-simulator evaluation preserves the ordering of policies and closely tracks real success; no coefficient given
note: Agreement claim is not quantified with a correlation metric.

name: REBOOT
evaluates: Precision assembly policies phase by phase (align and engage for pick, transport, align and engage for place) and their recovery from injected failures
improves: Real-world benchmarks reduce performance to binary success and datasets contain almost only successful demonstrations, hiding where precision tasks fail
setup: Real-robot dataset with four RGB-D viewpoints and language descriptions of phase success and failure; tasks annotated by symmetry, clearance tier and direction (install/remove pairs); half expert and half recovery demonstrations
scale: 2,160 demonstrations over 18 precision assembly tasks; baselines: action-chunked transformer, diffusion policy, π0-FAST, scored by phase-level completion rate
note: Abstract and part of the HTML opened; robot hardware and number of evaluation trials were not extracted.
